title: Solo 1H spear
author: Oathy
description:
# How to Play This Build

In this build, it's essential for you to understand **why you're picking things**. So, I'm dropping below a small list of when to use each skill, so you learn to think about why you should use them instead of using them just because I told you to use them in a specific matchup.

## 1. Weapon Skills

### Q — Q1

Use it whenever you can. Kite with it, deal damage, and keep things simple.

It's usually better against melee matchups and matchups where you need to create space.

### Q — Q2

You must use it in two specific situations:

1. **When an enemy blocks your path.** For example, a Fire Staff user with their Wall of Flames. Use it when someone can stay away from you and evade your auto-attacks (AA).
2. **When you can't brawl against your enemy.** This might be because they have significantly higher IP or because they're simply better at brawling and you would lose the trade.

---

### W — General Advice

**Quick advice:** If you master when to use each W, the difference between you and the average Spear user will be MASSIVE.

For this, here's the list.

#### W1 — PvE Only

You want to use this **ONLY for PvE**, for no other reason. W5 is simply better for PvP if you need more damage.

**Advice:** I recommend using this W only when you believe you're safe. Examples:

- You think the Mists you're in are empty.
- You're running a Solo Dungeon.

#### W2 — Situational Mobility

Just don't. It's SO bad.

Still, you can use it in some cases:

- **Running away:** If you need to run for a long time, equip it. With a bit of channeling, you can gain some movement speed, followed by another boost from the second proc.

Still, if you need to run and you're equipping this W, you should probably reconsider whatever you're about to do.

#### W3 — Mobility Buff Removal

This is the first W you'll mainly be using for PvP.

You want to use it against matchups that have speed buffs you can cleanse.

**Examples:**
- Double Swords: When they use Q on you, you can simply W to cleanse their charges.
- Rejuvenating Sprint.

I recommend learning when to use it offensively and defensively.

You don't want to use it just because an enemy is pressuring you with a small speed boost, only to use your boots afterward and get chased anyway. That would be bad, as you won't get them off you.

Sometimes, you must also wait a little before pressing it, because you might get a better opportunity.

#### W4 — Reflect

This W is a niche pick, but it's mandatory in specific situations.

You want to use it when:

- Enemies want to poke you or you can't do anything to prevent them from hitting you.
- You're fighting against burst-damage builds.

**Examples:**
- **Deathgivers:** They're about to double-E you. Proc W, and they might kill themselves.
- **Skystrider:** They proc E and hit you. They'll receive reflected damage, and you can still win even if you take one or two hits.

#### W5 — Main Damage Skill

This is the W you actually **WANT to have equipped for your fights**.

It provides:

- Slows.
- High damage.
- A hard-to-dodge ability.

This is just SO nice to use.

You should use it whenever it's not necessary or more convenient to use another W.

It works for:

- PvE.
- PvP.
- Pursuing light kiters.
- Damage checks.

It just feels nice. Trust me.

#### W6 — Heavy Kiting Matchups

You want to use this W against heavy kiters, such as:

- Chillhowls.
- 1H Frost Staff.
- Warbows.

You normally want to pair this W with Q2.

**Remember to think about your choice instead of picking skills mindlessly.** That way, you can land your W and leave the enemy crowd-controlled (CC'd) for a long time.

---

### E — Spirit Charges

You don't need to change this skill, but you must understand when and how to use it.

There are several ways to use E:

#### 1. Execute

Use it to finish kills while having **3 Spirit Charges** to secure the kill.

#### 2. Pursuing

Use it to close the distance and start brawling against enemies you want to fight in melee range.

#### 3. Escaping

Use it to create distance between yourself and your enemies.

#### 4. Extra Damage

In some cases, you might want to use E as a source of additional damage.

I can't cover every possible situation, but you'll learn them over time.

**Example:** You're fighting a Polehammer with Soldier Armor. Stack 2 Spirit Charges, then use E to create distance while dealing damage, allowing you to keep kiting.

#### 5. Intentionally Taking Damage to Prevent an Escape

If someone is about to escape and uses a skill that deals damage as part of their escape, you can E in front of them so they deal damage to you and become unable to escape afterward.

---

## 2. Off-Hand

This is a playstyle-based choice.

### Taproot
- Better for brawling.
- Provides more tankiness.

### Torch
- Slightly faster cooldowns.
- Slightly faster auto-attack speed.
- More overall damage.

---

## 3. Helmet

### Stalker Hood

If you're using Stalker Hood, you should use it in three situations.

#### 1. At the Start of a Long Fight

If you know a fight is going to last a long time, use it at the beginning.

The additional damage will be useful while you wait for the cooldown to come back before the enemy drops below 50% HP.

#### 2. As an E Combo Finisher

Use it to finish an enemy alongside E.

**Example:** The enemy is below 30% HP (these values depend on the matchup), and you have 3 Spirit Charges. Simply use your helmet skill and E to execute them.

#### 3. To Reveal Invisible Enemies

If you think you can hit an invisible enemy with it, use it. The enemy will be revealed.

### Mercenary Hood

You must know how to use it in two ways.

#### 1. Defensively

The enemy is about to deal a massive amount of damage to you. Proc it so you can withstand their damage.

You can also use it when you want to brawl, as the enemy will be at a disadvantage.

#### 2. Offensively

The enemy is trying to escape. Proc it so they get slowed and take damage.

---

## 4. Jacket

The question is: **Why should you pick one jacket over the other?**

The answer is simple.

### Specter Jacket
Choose it if you want a moderate increase in IP at a slightly higher price.

### Assassin Jacket
Choose it if you want to avoid paying extra for IP and prefer a slightly cheaper option.

### Inferno Shield

In both cases, **Inferno Shield is the better choice**.

You can use it to:

- Reflect damage.
- Reduce incoming damage.
- Win brawls.

During those 8 seconds, the enemy should avoid attacking you, or they'll get into trouble, unless they're using a non-reflectable skill or can simply withstand both you and Inferno Shield and out-DPS you anyway.

It's up to you to think about when these situations apply.

*Cough, cough... 1H Dagger with full damage.*

### Assassin Jacket — Ambush

With Assassin Jacket, you might find an interesting use for Ambush. Still, I wouldn't recommend it.

---

## 5. Boots

Normally, you want to use **Rejuvenating Sprint**.

However, against heavy kiters, if Harpoon isn't enough, you should consider picking the other skill.

These are simply Albion fundamentals:

- Gap closing.
- Health regeneration.
- Escaping.
- And other basic mobility utilities.

---

## 6. Cape

This depends on your playstyle, so just pick whichever suits you.

### Avalonian Cape
**Defensive.** Reduces the enemy's damage.

### Thetford Cape
**Offensive.** Its main purpose is to increase your damage.

---

## 7. Consumables

### Potions

#### PvP — Healing Potion

Just use Healing Potions. They're SO good.

They provide healing and can save you in clutch situations.

#### PvE / Escaping / High Danger — Invisibility Potion

You might want to use an Invisibility Potion to escape, whether you're:

- Roaming.
- Trying to flee from a ganker.
- In a zone with a ton of gankers.

### Food

Another playstyle-based choice.

#### Puremist — Brawling / Long Fights

Use it when you want to brawl or expect long fights.

#### Avalonian Stew — Kiting / Resetting / Short Fights

Use it when you want to kite, reset fights, or focus on shorter engagements.

title: Undying Gaze
author: Hiro
description:
Stillgaze may not be considered one of the strongest weapons in Albion, but I've always enjoyed its unique playstyle and wanted to build something around it that feels strong, fun, and genuinely my own.

This build focuses on sustained pressure, survivability, and outlasting opponents rather than relying on burst damage. Reality Fissure and Tether Shift provide consistent pressure while building toward the Crystal Cobra Transformation, while the defensive setup gives you the tools to survive enemy burst and continue fighting.

Cultist Robe, Undead Cape, high HP, and defensive cooldowns allow the build to reset fights and come back for another rotation. Raging Blink provides mobility for engaging or repositioning, while Levitate and Gigantify Potion give you additional ways to survive dangerous situations. Hellfire Potion can be used when you want more kill pressure.

The build is primarily designed for solo PvP and solo PvE, especially open-world content. It won't compete with meta weapons in raw efficiency, but that's not the point of this build. The goal is to make Stillgaze work through good timing, positioning, and repeated rotations.

Stillgaze is my main weapon, and this is the build I'm most passionate about. If you enjoy unconventional weapons and want to make something off-meta work, I hope you enjoy playing Undying Gaze as much as I do.

title: Dual Swords Open World Build
author: Ornlarf
description:
Gear and Ability Breakdown

Weapon: Dual Swords

Heroic Strike (Q): Your primary damage dealer. Builds Heroic Charges that boost your movement and attack speed.

Blade Cyclone (W): Provides excellent mobility and damage. It lets you spin through enemies, applying pressure or escaping tight spots.

Spinning Blades (E): Your heavy-hitting leap. It consumes Heroic Charges to deal massive area-of-effect (AoE) percentage-health damage and grants an attack speed/damage buff.

Deep Cuts (Passive): Every 4 auto-attacks, you apply a bleed effect. This adds constant tick damage.


Helmet: Helmet of Valor

Purifying Smoke (D): A highly tactical ability. It dispels enemy buffs (like their shields or boots) and removes crowd control or debuffs from you and your allies.

Toughness (Passive): Increases your armor and magic resistance to keep you surviving in close-range trades.


Armor: Mercenary Jacket

Bloodlust (R): The core mechanic of your sustain. When activated, every damage tick or auto-attack heals you for a flat amount (up to 7 times).

Balanced Mind (Passive): Provides a clean, passive increase to your raw damage and healing output.


Boots: Boots of Valor

Rejuvenating Sprint (F): A solid choice for catch-up or repositioning that heals you slightly over its duration.

Toughness (Passive): Adds another layer of baseline defenses.


Accessories & Consumables

Avalonian Cape: Automatically triggers on an auto-attack every few seconds, releasing a flash that lowers enemy damage and deals extra damage.

Gigantify Potion: Your panic button. It doubles your current and max health while making you immune to displacement effects, allowing you to survive heavy burst damage.

Beef Stew: Boosts your overall damage output by a flat percentage, ensuring your E-ability and basic attacks hit exceptionally hard.

title: Blazing Staff - Apagas 1
author: Einsemheim
description:
This build is designed **only for the initial engage**, unless it goes extremely well. It’s a **glass cannon**, so your goal is to deal massive damage and reset.  

**Engage Sequence:**  
1. **Prep** your **Royal Hood**  
2. **Pop** **Royal Sandals**, **Berserk Potion**, and **Scholar Robe**  
3. **Use E**, followed by **Fire Artillery**  

After that, reset unless the enemy team is severely weakened—**you die easily** if you overstay.  

**If You Die or Need to Swap:**  
- **Play defensively** and swap abilities to **Fire Wall, Burning Field, and Passive 1**  
- If you have a **strong healer or tank to peel**, you can keep pushing—the damage is so high it’s hard to counter without enemy support.  

**Important Note:**  
This is **not an ideal Crystal Arena build**—it's meant for fun. It **can work** and be devastating, but it’s too fragile for serious top-tier Arena matches.

title: Daybreaker Reflecting GOD
author: CallMeHAALAND
description:
How to play

1. Let your opponent use their big burst skill.
2. Activate Hunter Hood.
3. Use Deflecting Spin with your spear.
4. If the fight continues, activate Demon Armor.
5. Many opponents will damage themselves if they keep attacking during your reflect windows.

Is a 100% reflect build possible?

No. There is no equipment combination that gives permanent or complete (100%) reflect. Reflect abilities are temporary and have cooldowns, so success depends on timing rather than stacking every reflect effect. Reflected damage is also calculated before the target’s damage mitigation in most cases, making resistance buffs during your reflect window especially valuable.

title: Arclight Solo Mists Hunter (PvP/PvE) (Copy) (Copy)
author: Xuclamlatita
description:
​👤 Build Concept & Philosophy
​The golden rule of this set is strict budget management.
​High Budget / Confident Play: If you have enough silver and can comfortably afford at least 2–3 backup sets, go for the expensive, high-damage option. You must be confident in your PvP skills and play without fear.
​Low Budget / Eco Play: If these are your last resources, going out in expensive gear is a mistake. Fear of losing your items will cause you to choke and misplay during a fight. In this case, the build switches to a cheaper variant focused on survivability and sustain.
​
🛡️ Equipment & Skills

​1. Head: Plate Helmet (Helmet of Valor)
​Armor Type: Plate Helmet. Provides high base health and defense stats (superior to cloth or leather), significantly boosting your overall survivability.
​
Passive Skill: Increased Defense.

​Active Skill: Purge. Strips positive effects and buffs from the enemy, including invisibility. This is your key crowd control (CC) tool, allowing you to completely shut down the enemy's setup and turn the tide of a duel.
​
2. Chest: Choice Based on Budget
​
Option 1 (Expensive / Aggressive): Feyscale Robe
​Condition: Equip only if you have a solid silver cushion. It maximizes your damage output to force fast, aggressive fights.
​
Option 2 (Budget / Sustain): Mercenary Jacket
​Condition: Switch to this if you are on a tight budget or prefer a safer playstyle.
​Features: Leather armor provides a well-rounded balance of defense and resistances (which cloth robes lack). While your damage is slightly lower, the strategy completely shifts to sustaining through the third skill (Bloodlust) for damage and heavy healing. Depending on your preference, you can also optimize this setup for cooldown reduction.
​
3. Shoes: Royal Royal Shoes (Plate)
​Features: While plate shoes have access to the standard green skill (Refreshing Sprint for a small health regen), the choice here is the unique skill of the Royal Shoes.
​Skill: Offers a powerful burst of speed (strong acceleration) to easily catch up to running targets or gap-close.
​Drawbacks & Tactics: It has a long cooldown, but the massive mobility boost allows you to instantly lock down a target. Use it wisely while keeping the long cooldown in mind.
​
4. Cape: Smuggler's Cape (Bandit Cape)
​Core Mechanic: A unique cape tied to your potion slot usage.
​Effect: When you drink a potion (like a poison or a heal pot), the cape resets the cooldown of your potion slot, allowing you to use it consecutively.
​
5. Consumables: Health Regeneration Potions
​Choice: Healing potions that restore around 20–22% of your HP over a short duration.
​Tactics: Combined with the Smuggler's Cape, this grants you a double burst of heavy healing while you kite, reposition, and maneuver mid-combat.

title: Arclight Solo Mists Hunter (PvP/PvE)
author: TheV01D
description:
​👤 Build Concept & Philosophy
​The golden rule of this set is strict budget management.
​High Budget / Confident Play: If you have enough silver and can comfortably afford at least 2–3 backup sets, go for the expensive, high-damage option. You must be confident in your PvP skills and play without fear.
​Low Budget / Eco Play: If these are your last resources, going out in expensive gear is a mistake. Fear of losing your items will cause you to choke and misplay during a fight. In this case, the build switches to a cheaper variant focused on survivability and sustain.
​
🛡️ Equipment & Skills

​1. Head: Plate Helmet (Helmet of Valor)
​Armor Type: Plate Helmet. Provides high base health and defense stats (superior to cloth or leather), significantly boosting your overall survivability.
​
Passive Skill: Increased Defense.

​Active Skill: Purge. Strips positive effects and buffs from the enemy, including invisibility. This is your key crowd control (CC) tool, allowing you to completely shut down the enemy's setup and turn the tide of a duel.
​
2. Chest: Choice Based on Budget
​
Option 1 (Expensive / Aggressive): Feyscale Robe
​Condition: Equip only if you have a solid silver cushion. It maximizes your damage output to force fast, aggressive fights.
​
Option 2 (Budget / Sustain): Mercenary Jacket
​Condition: Switch to this if you are on a tight budget or prefer a safer playstyle.
​Features: Leather armor provides a well-rounded balance of defense and resistances (which cloth robes lack). While your damage is slightly lower, the strategy completely shifts to sustaining through the third skill (Bloodlust) for damage and heavy healing. Depending on your preference, you can also optimize this setup for cooldown reduction.
​
3. Shoes: Royal Royal Shoes (Plate)
​Features: While plate shoes have access to the standard green skill (Refreshing Sprint for a small health regen), the choice here is the unique skill of the Royal Shoes.
​Skill: Offers a powerful burst of speed (strong acceleration) to easily catch up to running targets or gap-close.
​Drawbacks & Tactics: It has a long cooldown, but the massive mobility boost allows you to instantly lock down a target. Use it wisely while keeping the long cooldown in mind.
​
4. Cape: Smuggler's Cape (Bandit Cape)
​Core Mechanic: A unique cape tied to your potion slot usage.
​Effect: When you drink a potion (like a poison or a heal pot), the cape resets the cooldown of your potion slot, allowing you to use it consecutively.
​
5. Consumables: Health Regeneration Potions
​Choice: Healing potions that restore around 20–22% of your HP over a short duration.
​Tactics: Combined with the Smuggler's Cape, this grants you a double burst of heavy healing while you kite, reposition, and maneuver mid-combat.

title: Twin Slayers 1v3 Depths
author: Itstacotaco
description:
Full Combo: 
R > Q > AA > W > E > D > Q > E

Combo Explained:
PHASE 1 - Stacking Bonus Damage
R - Armor gives 9% damage per stack (max 8) you'll want to start stacking this as soon as you start taking damage to get to 72% bonus damage
Q - This is mostly for positioning and to start stacking daggers bonus damage passive
AA - This will proc your Ava Cape and reduce damage dealt by players hit by 15%. Imporant to do early to reduce damage taken while your R is stacking
W - be as close to the enemy as possible so that all 3 blades hit your target for max damage output. If possible, try and hit 2 additional targets to get extra bonus damage (10% bonus damage per target hit, max 3)

PHASE 2 - The Execute
E - At this point your should be full buffed with as much bonus damage as possible. You need to finish the combo quickly. Use your first E to send the daggers out and increase movement speed.
D - Stun the enemy (hopefully multiple enemies) so that you can set up your second E.
Q - This is only for positioning. If you are already in the best position then skip this step.
E - While standing directly ontop of your enemy, pull your blades back and this should kill any enemy without defensives or heals. 

PHASE 3 - Reset
If the enemy countered your combo or you've messed up, do not hang around. You have long cooldowns (25s, 30s, 35s). Get out as fast as you can while you get your cooldowns back.
F - Run towards the best exit. (TIP) Don't use Q while you have movespeed buff. Wait until it ends.
1 - Use anytime the enemy is about to close the distance on you. Best use is around corners. 

Things to know:
- Auto Attack (AA) early to proc cape and reduce enemy damage by 15%
- Cast W at close range to deal more damage
- Hit 3 targets with W for max Bonus Damage
- AoE (Area of Effect) Escalation: More players hit = More damage dealt 
- Get in, Get out. Don't hang around. You aren't built to brawl.
- Do not use boots to engage, only to kite, if needed
- Use potion only to kite
- Twin Slayers are not easy to play. It's takes a while to master. Don't get impatient or frusterated.

description:
# Bow of Badon

Hardest **DPS** to play. The reason being your **E skill** is hardest to land compared to other **DPS**.

## Gears and Skills

### Main Weapon

#### Bow of Badon

Used mainly for the **interrupt**, especially for the **Callous Occultists** aka **Witches**.

#### Bow of Badon skills

Q skill **Multishot**, W skill **Explosive Arrows**, E skill **Raging Storm**. Passive **Energetic** or **Piercing Arrows**.

### Head Piece

#### Specter Hood/Assasin Hood

Either one is good.

#### Specter Hood/Assasin Hood skills

**Flash of insight** for **SH**, **Meditation** for **AH**. Passive **Quick Thinker**.

### Chest Piece

#### Royal Jacket

Both **Shadow Caller** and **Bow of Badon** usually on **Royal Jacket** for faster cooldowns.

#### Royal Jacket skills

R skill **Royal Banner**, passive **Quick Thinker**.

### Leg Piece

#### Stalker Shoes

**SS** for extra damage and better dodge.

#### Stalker Shoes skills

**Raging Blick** and **Quick Thinker**.

### Cape

#### Lymhurst Cape

Makes you self sufficient with **energy**.

## How to play

### Pre-stacking buffs

#### Royal Robe

Maximum **passive damage bonus** you can get from **Cloth Robes** is a total of **58%**. **50%** from stats and **8%** from **Agression** passive skill. Compare it to the **Leather Jackets** **20-30%**. In particular **Royal Jacket** is **25% damage bonus**. You can get **30%** bonus from **6 stacks** of **RR**, that will top you up to total of **55%**, which is only **3%** less than if you were on the **Cloth Robe**.

#### Stalker Shoes

Additional **16% damage**.


### Landing E

The timing of **E skill** is immediately after mobs clumped.

Avoid hitting bats and other mobs that stand between you and the mob clump with your **E skill**. Launching **E skill** too early can sometimes miss it. Try to **interrupt** mobs before they use their skills.

### W and Q

**W** and **Q** after **E skill**.

**CS** for debuff and faster mobs clearing, **SS** for extra damage and better dodge capabilities. If not sure what to use go for **SS**.

#### Cultist Sandals/Stalker Shoes skills

**Rotten Ground** and **Agression** for **CS**. **Raging Blick** and **Quick Thinker** for **SS**.

### Cape

#### Lymhurst Cape/Demon Cape

**LC** Makes you self sufficient with **energy**. **DC** for extra damage.

## How to play


### Pre-stacking buffs

#### Royal Robe

Maximum **passive damage bonus** you can get from **Cloth Robes** is a total of **58%**. **50%** from stats and **8%** from **Agression** passive skill. Compare it to the **Leather Jackets** **20-30%**. In particular **Royal Jacket** is **25% damage bonus**. You can get **30%** bonus from **6 stacks** of **RR**, that will top you up to total of **55%**, which is only **3%** less than if you were on the **Cloth Robe**.

#### Stalker Shoes

Additional **16% damage**.

### Landing E

Timing of you E Skill **Inner Shadow** is really important. When you see **tank** using W skill **Air Compressor** you should immediately press **E skill**. Ideally **Inner Shadow's** animation ends right after mobs get clumped.

To avoid getting hit you can just pass through the mob clump a couple of  times instead of standing still on the clump the whole time. **CS** trail lasts **2.2 seconds** and the debuff itself lasts **3 seconds** after mobs leave the trail.

title: Incubus Mace Tank Morgana Static Dungeon Build
author: whitefirewolf
description:
# Tank 

Hardest Role to play. Need to know every pull by the heart, know how to dodge the mob's skills and keep aggro.

## Gears and Skills

### Main Weapon

#### Incubus mace

I tried all other maces and none of them as good as **Incubus mace**. The **Shrinking Curse** E skill of the **Incubus** have **20% Max and Current Health Reduction** and  **Damage Dealt reduction by 40%** which is overpowered.

#### Incubus mace skills

Q skill on **Threatening Smash**, W skill  **Air Compressor**, E skill **Shrinking Curse**. I like passive on **Energetic** but can be anything.

### Offhand

#### Astral Aegis/Sarcophagus

**Astral Aegis** and **Sarcophagus** clumping mobs nicely, if you go other off-hand for example **Leering Cane** mobs going to spread all over the place after your W **Air Compressor** skill.

### Head Piece

#### Soldier Helmet/Mistwalker Hood

Both are good. Matter of preference. Personal choice is **Soldier Helmet** because it can deny mob's **damage and CC** but with **Fallen Staff's** E skill **Salvation** the **Mistwalker Hood** might be most optimal, especially when comparing **D skill cooldowns**. **SH** **40 seconds** versus **MH** **25 seconds**. Another argument in favor of **MH** might be skill duration **5 seconds** versus **SH** **2.5 seconds**.

#### Soldier Helmet/Mistwalker Hood skills

D skill **Block** for **Soldier Helmet**, passive is **Toughness**. **Immortal** and **Quick Thinker/Balanced Mind** for **Mistwalker Hood**.

### Chest Piece

#### Guardian Armor/Any plate armor

**Plate armor** is a must for a tank as it has highest **Defence**, **Armor**, **Magical Resistance** and **Max Health** . Tank on **Plate armor** always going to take reduced damage from mobs compared to the **Leather Armor** or **Cloth Armor**.

#### Guardian Armor/Any plate armor skills

Most popular armor is a **Guardian Armor** as it has **Enfeeble Aura** R skill which **Reduces damage of affected enemies by 60%**. It's especially useful during big pulls. If you using any other plate armor you should use **Taunt** R skill, which helps with holding the aggro. **Thoughness** on the first passive, **Protective Instinct** on the second. **Protective Instinct** increases your **Threat Generation by 400%**, without it you probably will not be able to hold aggro as a tank.


### Leg Piece

#### Royal Boots

**Royal Boots** have a good **speed and speed duration** combination. All other boots are either too slow or doesn't last that long for tank to do big pulls effectively.

#### Royal Boots skills

**Royal March** F skill and **Toughness** passive.

### Cape

**Martlock Cape** for extra defenses during big pulls or **Caerleon Cape** for that additional **Q skill** to keep a mob's aggro better.

## How to Play

### Getting speed buff

As a tank you start with F skill **Royal March** and get **10 stacks** on your speed buff. Getting maximum bonus will help you do more cleaner pulls. In general you never want to do slow pulls.

### Pulling the mobs

 After you got your speed buff use Q skill **Threatening Smash** on the first group of mobs you want to pull and run straight to the second group. Try to spam your **Q skill** on the mobs, it helps with increasing your **Threat** towards the mobs. The more **Threat** you have,  the lower the chance you will lose aggro. After that W skill  **Air Compressor** and immediatedly **Soldier Helmet's** D **Block** skill or **Mistwalker Hood's** **Immortal**. If you using **SH** you will need to cancel it after around **1 second** in order to use your **E skill**.

### Debuff

After mobs clumped immediately use your E skill **Shrinking Curse** on the clumped mobs and continue spamming your Q skill on cooldown in order to keep the aggro. If some of the mobs chasing **DPS** or **Healer** use **Taunt** R skill on them. The mobs should die in one rotation.

### Secret to clean pulls

Secret to clean pulls is your running path. Sometimes you will see mobs walking into clump themselves even when not clumped by **Air Compressor**, the reason is if you go far enough from them they forced to chase you. In general for example if there is 2 group of mobs you start by aggroing first group with Q **Threatening Smash**  then running to the edge of the second group and then back to the far edge of the first and back to the center and then press W **Air Compressor**, mobs should clump nicely. Same for 3 or more groups.

### Threat

Spam your **Q ability** on cooldown, it increases your threat. Mobs attack the player who has the highest threat value. You can also spam your R **Taunt**, but i like to keep it for the **Dark Paladin's** skill that changes all mobs aggro.

### Shadowcaller Debuff

Make sure most of the mobs are close to you when the **Shadowcaller** E **Inner Shadow** skill hits, otherwise debuff not going to work. You can even let yourself get hit by mob's skills if it helps you with landing the debuff on the mobs.

### Big Pulls

If you doing big pulls make sure to alternate between big and medium pulls, so healer have their **Graveguard Helmet** D **Sacrifice** skill's cooldown ready.

description:
# Blazing

Easiest to play.

## Gears and Skills

### Main Weapon

#### Blazing Staff

Top DPS.

#### Blazing Staff skills

Q skill **Burning Field**, W skill **Raging Flare** or **Fire Wave**, E skill **Flame Tornado**. Passive **Energetic** or **Furious**.

### Head Piece

#### Assasin Hood

Assasin Hood used to decrease **cooldown** of the **Blazing's** E skill **Flame Tornado**. **Flame Tornado** has one of the longest cooldowns of **35 seconds**, compare it to the **Shadowcaller's** **30 seconds**, **Bow of Badon's** **30 seconds** and Tank's **Soldier Helmet's** D skill **Block's** cooldown of **40 seconds** .

#### Assasin Hood skills

**Meditation** D skill and passive **Quick Thinker**.

### Chest Piece

#### Royal Robe/Druid Robe

**Royal Robe** or **Druid Robe** depending on what **Healer** is wearing. If **Healer** on **RR** use **DR** and vice versa.

#### Royal Robe/Druid Robe skills

**Magic Rune** for **RR's** R skill, passive **Aggression** or **Efficiency**. **Obsessive Burst** for **Druid Robe** and passive is same as **RR**.

### Leg Piece

#### Royal Sandals/Stalker Shoes

**Leg Piece** used for extra damage buff, but any shoes works if damage is enough without it. **Royal Sandals** gives total of **18,5%** additional damage. **15%** from the **Defenseless Rush** and **3,5%** from **Agression** passive. **Stalker Shoes** gives **16%** bonus if you stack **2 times** and also have great potential for dodging mob's skills with blink compared to **RS**. **SS** Also have better cooldown **25 seconds** vs **RS's** **30 seconds**.

#### Royal Sandals/Stalker Shoes skills

**Defenseless Rush** and **Agression** for **Royal Sandals**. **Raging Blink** and **Quick Thinker** for **Stalker Shoes**. 

### Cape

#### Lymhurst Cape

**Blazing Staff** users run out of energy quickly. Use **Energetic** weapon passive and/or **Efficiency** on cloth armor in case you experience any problems with **energy**.

## How to play

### Pre-stacking the buffs

#### Royal Robe

If you using **Royal Robe** you need to know the time and place on when and where to drop it.  Ideally you would get **6 stacks** of the **Magic Rune's** buff. Each stack is **5%**, so total would be **30%** additional **Magical Damage**.

**RR** reduces **Cast time by 10%** for each stack, so maximum bonus can be **60%**, which will help you to cast your E skill **Flame Tornado** much faster.

#### Druid Robe

For **Druid Robe** your **damaget and healing cast** increased by **6%** every time you cast a spell and it stacks up to **6 times**, so maximum bonus you can get is **36%**. I find it hard to get maximum bonus with **Druid Robe** compared to **Royal Robe**. As blazing it is enough to get 1-2 stacks or **Druid Robe** before using **E skill**, just make sure you get 6 stacks on **RR**.

#### Royal Shoes/Stalker Shoes

You have **7 seconds** buff on **RS** and **4.5 seconds** on **SS**. You should time it so you will get all your buffs stacked when **E skill** is cast.

### Dropping E damage

Use your **E** on the mobs after tank clumps them with **Air Compressor**. 

#### E skill timing

If **Shadow Caller** knows it's timing they going to **press** their **E** skill **Inner Shadow** immediately after tank **pressed W skill** **Air Compressor**. **Air Compressor** have a delay of **1,5 seconds** same as **SC's Inner Shadow**, so if **SC's** timing is right you going to see **Inner Shadow's** animation end right after mobs clump, that's when you need to drop your **E skill**.

### Q and W

Use **Q and W** to finish off the mobs.

title: Fallen Staff Healer Morgana Static Dungeon Build
author: whitefirewolf
description:
# Healer

Second hardest role to play after the tank.

## Gears and Skills

### Main Weapon

#### Fallen Staff/Any Holy Staff except Great Holy

Any healing staff works except **Great Holy Staff**, it has knockback so it's bad for PVE in general. Current meta is **Fallen Staff**.

With the **Fallen Staff** buff it became new meta both in **PVE** and **ZVZ**. **2 second** immunity to damage, great amount of **Health recovered** and **CC, debuff and DOT** cleanse going to make your life much easier as a healer.

#### Holy Staff's skills

Q skill **Holy Flash**, W skill **Holy Beam**, and each E skill for respective **Holy Staff**. Passive should be on **Ascended** in order to make your W skill **uninterrruptable**.

### Offhand

If you using one handed **Holy Staff** use **Celestial Censer** for extra **Healing Cast Bonus**.

### Head Piece

#### Graveguard Helmet

Healer needs to be on **Graveguard Helmet** for emergency heals for a **Tank**.

#### Graveguard Helmet's skills

D skill **Sacrifice**. Passive **Toughness**.

### Chest Piece

#### Royal Robe/Druid Robe

**Royal Robe** or **Druid Robe** depending on what **Blazing Staff** DPS is wearing. If **Blazing** on **RR** use **Druid** and vice versa. If as a healer you struggling and getting damage you can use **Cleric Robe**.

#### Royal Robe/Druid Robe skills

**Magic Rune** for **RR's** R skill, passive **Aggression** or **Efficiency**. **Obsessive Burst** for **Druid Robe** and passive is same as **RR**.

### Leg Piece

#### Stalker Shoes

Any shoes can work if you use **Dodge** aka **Dogde Roll**. **Stalker Shoes** adds extra **16% Healing Cast** which is going to make healing much easier. Use  **Cleric Sandals** or **any other shoes** if you don't want to prestack the **Stalker Shoes's** buff. The F **Blink** skill on **Cleric Sandals** helps to avoid mob's skills and damage fast.

#### Stalker Shoes skills

**Raging Blink** and **Quick Thinker**.

### Cape

#### Lymhurst Cape

Makes you self sufficient with **energy**.

## How to play

### Pre-stacking the buffs

If you using **Royal Robe** you need to know the time and place on when and where to drop it. Ideally you would get **6 stacks** of the **Magic Rune's** buff. Each stack is **5%**, so total would be **30%** additional **Healing Cast**. In addition to that if you using **Stalker Shoes** the total bonus would be **46% Healing Cast** not counting other bonuses.

For **Druid Robe** your **damage and healing cast** increased by **6%** every time you cast a spell and it stacks up to 6 times, so maximum bonus you can get is **36%**, but I find it hard to get maximum bonus with **Druid Robe** compared to **Royal Robe**.

### Using healing skills

#### Fallen Staff

Open with **E skill** **Salvation**. It has **1 second** **Cast time** during which you can be interrupted, so you need to be careful not to stay near the **Dark Paladin**. After that the **E skill** has **2 second** delay. You need to know on where to drop your **E skill**. Ideally healer knows which pulls tank is doing and can predict on where mobs and tank is going to be.

After that **W**, **Q** and **D** if necessary. 

#### Any other Staff

Start with W **Holy Beam** skill right after **Tank** clumps the mobs with **Air Compressor**. Don't use any healing skills before **Tank** gets the aggro and be careful not to heal too early otherwise aggro is going to be on you.

After W **Holy Beam** if sustain not enough use your D **Sacrifice** if tank is too low on health or E skill. If you using **Hallowfall** be careful not to jump into mob's skills, sometimes they can stun you and oneshot.

 If pulls correct and DPS know how to dodge you don't need to use any skills on DPS except Q **Holy Flash**, keep most of your sustain for the tank, expecially W **Holy Beam**. If **Tank** goes down usually mobs go for the healer next.

 ### Getting W's Holy Beam's cooldown

**DPS** with **Royal Jacket** should use **R Royal Banner** skill immediately after dropping **E skills**, if you stand inside it's range your **Holy Beam's** cooldown going to be much lower and you can sustain **Tank** much better.

title: Holy Staff Healer Hellgate 2v2 Helm of Valor Build
author: MomoMonii
description:
*Budget version of this build is swapping to mercenary shoes, but both robes arguably equally useful*

### Skill Swaps (vs Heal/DPS)
*In almost all situations you should run ascended passive if running Beam unless there is no interrupt or forced movement on enemy*
* Frost Shield against most Ranged DPS - except: Use Purge against Curse running grudge, Purge against Druidic Robe and Purity Robe against  Demonic
* Use Purge on Robe if enemy DPS has clearly purgeable buffs: Claymore, Deadly Swipe (Q2) Dagger Pair, Druid Robe, Feyscale Robe
* Against Heavy Crossbow - Pulse + Roll - Use pulse to interrupt sunder (or autofire if needed) and roll to dodge the Debuff, care not to purge your royal cowl using pulse
* Axe - Pulse to keep distance unless this interferes with your DPS playstyle and Refreshing Sprint
* 1h Curse - Pulse to try to interrupt E and Refreshing Sprint or Roll (if running cleanse pot roll may not be necessary)
* Demonic - Beam and Refreshing Sprint
* Rotcaller - Beam and Refreshing Sprint or Roll (E Debuff can be dodged with roll)
* Dagger Pair - Blessing and After Image
* Claymore - Blessing and After Image (After image can be used to dodge E if timed well)
* One Shot Imp - Frost Shield, Pulse and Roll (uses pulse after pulled in and then dodge roll helm or use pulse to interrupt Hellfire Barrage) (use Roll against Polymorph to dodge transformation)  

### Skill Swaps (Double DPS or One Shot)
* Refreshing Sprint for most matchups, Roll or After Image can be good against Gloves
* Beam against big damage where you expect them to go on DPS and you are running Refreshing Sprint
* Blessing otherwise

### Potion Swaps
* T7 Resistance Potion against Double DPS or One Shot where cleanse is not as useful and as default against Heal/DPS
* T7 Cleanse pot as default and against One Shot that has a lot of stun - if you see royal helm or combinations like 1h Dagger and Staff of Balance or Grailseeker
* T7 Cleanse pot against Heal/DPS 1h Curse, Rotcaller, or Hellfire Hands
* T6 Energy Pot against Heal/DPS Purging builds - If DPS has fiend cowl or helm of valor or is running a weapon that can purge like daybreaker, lifecurse, 1h arcane

title: Holy Staff Solo Build
author: Uanes
description:
The Holy Staff build is an excellent choice for solo play in Albion, as it provides both damage and the ability to stay alive for a long time, whether in PvE content or even PvP.

With the Holy Staff, your Q is your main source of damage, along with your W, which not only deals damage but also heals a small amount of your HP. The E ability heals instantly based on your current health; if your health is below 40%, the heal will be greater.

Your Guardian Helmet will be your greatest defense, thanks to its shield ability. Use it when the enemy is dealing constant damage to you, or to counter an ability with massive damage. If you run low on mana, you can switch your helmet’s ability to the first one.

Your Mage Robe serves to add defense and, most importantly, dispel enemy buffs, such as dispelling the Mercenary’s Chest, Cleric’s Chest, or even the Guardian’s Helmet. However, remember that for the enemy to lose the buff, they must deal damage to you while your robe is active.

Your Scholar Sandals are for mana regeneration, and primarily to help when you need to move more quickly.

title: Bow of Badon (DPS) - Group Dungeon
author: ToasterOwO
description:
### Combo:
Use R at the very start to help everyone stack up. You simply use your E, follow up with QQ and then W. Once you have a moment use your hood to reset cooldown and repeat.

### Words of Wisdom:
You're the support here, so make sure to be there on time to use your Robe so everyone can benefit from the damage increase.

Remember to bring Druid Cowl as a swap in-case the shadowcaller leaves the party or isn't needed.

Any leather shoe works, you only need to spring and get there on time for the pull.

title: Fallen Staff (Healer) - Group Dungeon
author: ToasterOwO
description:
### Combo:
E > W > QQ (Regular)
E > D > W > QQ (If Tank/healer makes a mistake)
Use Jacket if you're stuck on CD and the tank needs healing as soon as possible. Otherwise just use at the end of the fight.

### Words of Wisdom:
You may ignore any and all DPS, they are stupid and should dodge on their own. Only heal with Q skill when you're in a calm situation where tank and yourself is at full health and you have spare skills on hand. 

Any leather shoe works. (Can do Plate or Cloth as well but leather is recommended)

title: Mistpiercer (DPS) - Group Dungeon
author: ToasterOwO
description:
### Combo:
Start with Q, then spam E, then W to do basic attack. If you get a moment, use your hood to reset cooldown and repeat.

### Words of Wisdom:
Try to angle it right so that you don't aggro all of Wakanda with your arrows. You may also replace the cape for something else like Caerleon if you're broke.

Can use any leather or cloth shoes.

title: Bow of Badon (DPS) - Static Dungeon
author: ToasterOwO
description:
### Combo:
Use E to start then Q two times due to the cape follow up with W to basic attack. Once the mobs drop to 50% health get close to them and use D to use the hood and move back to safety.

### Words of Wisdom:
In Simp Army Dungeon you must target the bats with Q skill and avoid them or else miss E skill. When fighting the Halberd Boss from the Simp Army don't use E skill as it'll cause the boss to jump and one shot your party. Your Royal Jacket can be used as the 2nd one, let Shadowcaller use his first and then you do your once the fight ends.

Any leather shoe works, you only need a dodge skill.

title: Shadowcaller (Support) - Group Dungeon / Static Dungeon
author: ToasterOwO
description:
### Combo:
Use your E within a moment you see the Tank is using "Air Pressure" as it takes a while for your skill to drop. Make sure you're targeting in on top of the Tank to hit all the mobs. Your other priority is to use R to help the healer with cooldown and helmet to drop mana for everyone.

### Words of Wisdom:
Make sure to be the first one to use your jacket skill and if you see overlap, point out that you'll be the first one to use it. You may also help tank by bringing in more mobs if they are too far away or end up running away but do it based on the situation and demand.

Any Leather and Cloth shoe work.

title: Blazing Staff (DPS) - Static Dungeon
author: ToasterOwO
description:
### Combo:
Royal Sandal: Q Q R W E > R
Stalker Shoe: F F R W E > Q Q R

With Royal Sandal you drop the QQ skill on random place to stack up then R to active more buff. Then you use W on the target and E afterwards. R to reset your cooldown and continue as is.

With Stalker Shoe you FF skill on random place to stack up then R to active more buff. Then you use W on the target and E afterwards. Before you reset you can drop QQ skill 2 times due to the cape and then R to reset your cooldown and continue as is.

### Words of Wisdom:
You're the main damage dealer of the party so remember to keep calming close as if the tank gets knocked out the next target will almost always be you.

title: Incubus Mace (Tank) - Group Dungeon / Static Dungeon
author: ToasterOwO
description:
### Combo:
Either of the helmet works here. Soldier helmet gives better sustain as you run around while mistwalker hood helps you do bigger pull which is ideal for static. You want to start it off with your boots skill, once you get the first batch of mobs use your armor skill then get more. When all are together use "air pressure" to put them in place and use E on them.

For boss fight it is wise to swap to Guard Rune to protect from large damage or CC skills.

### Words of Wisdom:
Take your time when doing it, if you rush you're the one who'll get the repair bill. The dps and healer can usually run away. Use your helmet skill wisely, it can be before or after you use air pressure based on how much damage you're taking. Omelette is better for lower cd thus quicker pulls while sandwich keeps you alive if you're starting out and getting the hang of it.

Use R at the very beginning when tank starts running to get mobs attention you drop the skill to help others and yourself stack up. title: Zylphire's Comp | Incubus Tank
author: Zylphire
description:
First Slot Ability

Defensive Slam
The safest and most consistent first slot ability. It increases damage reduction and CC resistance. Mobs can hit hard and very often have very annoying crowd control abilities, and this ability often enables you to survive when making mistakes.

Threatening Smash
Not a bad option, but it's never the best. Increases threat to mobs hit by 100. The extra threat can feel a bit unnecessary since you will be using Taunt. Works well when multiple mobs are guarding the track.

Sacred Ground
Very situational but high-impact. Against certain tracking targets (e.g., Dawnbird, Golem, Imp), temporarily disabling certain abilities makes the fights go faster or easier/safer.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Second Slot Ability

Ground Shaker
Currently the best second slot ability due to a lack of strong competition aside from niche scenarios. Provides good raw damage along with a knockup to disrupt the target's channeling abilities.

Snare Charge
Mainly used for mobility, which is only worth taking when tracking werewolves to take the blood puddles.

Guard Rune
Previously the best defensive option, but it got nerfed and now has lower damage resistance. Only useful when you need immunity to crowd control or forced movement (e.g., Direbear, Golem).

Air Compressor
Can be used to pull tracking targets, particularly if you don't have Fiend Sandals. Works well when multiple mobs are guarding the track while having a party with decent AoE damage.

Weapon Passive

Energetic
The only real option for passive ability. Provides a small boost to mana sustain. Remember to auto-attack to activate it.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Off-Hand

Mistcaller
Best-in-slot. Reduces cooldowns, allowing for faster skill rotations.

Any Shield
Good defensive option. Provides extra survivability. Avoid Astral Aegis, as it hurts mana sustain.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Helmets

Hellion Hood
Provides the best utility by cancelling or delaying key abilities of tracking targets. Examples include delaying Golem's turtle mode and removing werewolf blood puddles.

Assassin Hood
Works better with less optimal teams by allowing more uses of your Incubus ultimate, improving consistency.

Mercenary Hood
A very good defensive option. Reduces enemy damage by 30% and interrupts channeling abilities.

Stalker Hood
A weaker option, somewhat usable. Provides resistance reduction when enemies are below 50% HP, generally better suited for DPS roles.

Passive

Quick Thinker
The only real option for passive ability. Provides a small cooldown rate boost.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Armors

Any plate armor works since you'll be using Taunt for most encounters.

Judicator Armor
A good defensive option, especially when Taunt is less effective on some tracking targets (e.g., Golem, Imp, Ent, Shadowmask). Grants additional damage resistance and increases healing received by 30%.

Armor Passive

Toughness
The only real option for passive ability. Provides a small boost to survivability.

Armor Second Passive

Spirit Crush
The default choice. Normal attacks apply a debuff on mobs, reducing max health by 12%.

Protective Instinct
Increases threat generation by 400%. Can be used if you're struggling with maintaining aggro, but it's generally unnecessary since you have Taunt.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Shoes

Fiend Sandals
Allows you to swap targets with a target (ally or enemy), disrupting channeling abilities. Which can be used offensively or defensively. Very useful against tracking targets who move a lot (e.g., Shadowmask, Dawnbird, Direbear).

Cultist Sandals
Provides resistance reduction on boots. Mainly used for DPS, viable if your group lacks it.

Any Leather Shoes
Refreshing sprint helps a little bit with the cooldown reduction, helping a little bit with ability uptime. 

Passive

Efficiency
Provides a small boost to mana sustain.

Ask questions here: https://discord.gg/WdZbsfhre

title: Beginner 3v3 Depths Claymore
author: Gremmy
description:
Weapon: You can swap Claymore with Carving Sword or Kingmaker once you feel comfortable playing swords. Auto attack to apply your passive and Q to gain stacks. Once you have 3 stacks, press E on your target if they have no active defenses. Use your W once they are stunned only if you are sure your target will die. This is an important gap-closing skill that should be saved to close the gap, not just to do damage. If you use it purely for damage, but then get denied multiple Qs/AAs, you have lost out on DPS. Switch to Q2 when clearing mob camps. 

Head: Valor helmet is an AOE purge/cleanse that you can use to cleanse your allies and yourself of crowd-control effects and debuffs, or purge enemy abilities such as cleric robes or sprints. You will often purge a defensive ability right before you E. Tenacity hood is a massive healing reduction on anyone who steps in the puddle you place on the ground. Use this right after you E to ensure it hits and secures kills despite healers. Swap to cleanse or energy shield on the Tenacity hood if there are no healers on the enemy team. 

Chest: Everlasting Spirit on your Cleric Robe works well against most comps (Claymore, Bow of Badon) in the Depths, especially one-shot comps. Frost Shield is ideal against damage over time comps (Rotcaller, Regular Bow). Mage robe has a purging shield which is an excellent defensive that can purge enemy sword stacks, regular bow Es, and other critical abilities. 

Shoes: You will usually start the fight by using your Energizing Sprint to close the gap on your target, such as the enemy healer. You can use any cloth sandal for this ability. 

Cape: Martlock cape is the best cape. Thetford cape is really good for higher damage pressure. 

Potion: Resistance potion is your longest defensive cooldown aside from Martlock cape. You will usually use Resistance potion after your armor ability is purged or runs out, or pre-resistance potion when the enemy is being super aggressive, to mitigate the initial burst. 

Food: 15% damage increase. Yeah.

title: Beginner 3v3 Depths Bow
author: Gremmy
description:
Weapon: Spam your abilities as soon as they come off cooldown to keep consistent pressure on your opponents. Regular Bow damage basically never has to stop. You can split focus to start fights, but make sure to focus on the same targets your melee DPS is when they E.

Head: You can use any hood for a cleanse, but if there isn't the need for a cleanse in a fight, you can always swap over to Flash of Insight to double how many times you can use your chest piece. Cleanse can remove armor debuffs and end crowd-control effects. Valor helmet is an AOE purge/cleanse that you can use to cleanse your allies and yourself of crowd-control effects and debuffs, or purge enemy abilities such as cleric robes or sprints. You'll want to be positioned back near (but not directly on top of) the healer so that you can use these abilities on them. 

Chest: Everlasting Spirit on your Cleric Robe works well against most comps (Claymore, Bow of Badon) in the Depths, especially one-shot comps. Frost Shield is ideal against damage over time comps (Rotcaller, Regular Bow). Mage Robe is an excellent defensive to purge enemy sword stacks, regular bow Es, and other critical abilities. 

Shoes: Use Refreshing sprint to reposition yourself to safety or to secure a kill. You can switch over to Blind Spot for more damage and self-protection. 

Cape: Martlock cape is the best cape. Thetford Cape is really good for higher damage pressure, especially alongside Blind Spot on your shoes. 

Potion: Resistance potion is your longest defensive cooldown aside from Martlock cape. You will usually use Resistance potion after your armor ability is purged or runs out, or pre-resistance potion when the enemy is being super aggressive, to mitigate the initial burst. 

Food: 15% damage increase. Yeah.

title: Beginner 3v3 Depths Holy Healer
author: Gremmy
description:
Weapon: Your E, when used, places a buff on you that increases your healing by 5%, stacking up to 3 times for a total of 15% increased healing. You should spam this ability just before that buff runs out to maintain this healing buff in case you unexpectedly enter into combat. Your 4th passive is crucial if opponents have a way to interrupt your W. You can change it to 1st passive if you are fighting a team without a way to interrupt your W. Hallowfall is an okay weapon to use instead, but you will miss out on healing in favor of a skill that can keep you alive (Hallowfall E dash). 

Off-Hand: Whether you use Sarcophagus or Mistcaller is up to your personal preference. I would recommend that you use Sarcophegus to start and then branch out until you become more comfortable with Depths fights. 

Head: This ability makes your mana costs 0 for the duration. If you use it as soon as it comes off cooldown, it will be active 50% of the time. This ability ensures that you don't immediately run out of mana.

Chest: Everlasting Spirit on your Cleric Robe works well against most comps (Claymore, Bow of Badon) in the Depths, especially one-shot comps. Frost Shield is ideal against damage over time comps (Rotcaller, Regular Bow). Mistwalker jacket is an excellent, though expensive, option. It makes you immune for a long period of time, and when you aren't being targeted, you can cast a few spells to keep your team up during the duration and the immunity will almost immediately come back online. 

Shoes: Use Refreshing Sprint to move away from the enemy DPS. Usually, you can run through them and past the enemy healer, making it so that the enemy DPS have to run through your DPS to get to you. The same can be done with Dodge roll, which you can also save to dodge crucial abilities (Carving E, Bear Paws E). Use Mercenary shoes to break out of crowd-control effects or leap to safety when there are no crowd-control threats. Use Mistwalker Shoes to dash away from your team early in a fight to keep yourself safe. Reactivate the dash to return and heal your teammates. Use your dash to lead opponents away from your marked location to create time for your DPS to win the fight.

Cape: Martlock cape is the best cape.

Potion: Resistance potion is your longest defensive cooldown aside from Martlock cape. You will usually use Resistance potion after your armor ability is purged or runs out. 

Food: Avalonian Omelets are the best food. Regular omelets are fine on a budget.

In melee matchups, go with the helmet's second skill

description:

Goal is to run with group or play solo

PVE

PvP

Typical fight proceedure is to stand further back from engaging team, not too far where you cannot 'Divine Intervention' into the fight to stop ongoing channeled damage.

If you can heal the DPS without putting the tank at risk, do so, but the tank is the priority.                                    -DPS are assumed to dodge damage; if a DPS takes damage from an area, it is their responsibility and not the tank's or yours as the healer.       

*Aggro Management:
-It is crucial that you do not heal the tank before he "hits" monsters with an ability (Q, E or W). If you do, you will steal aggro from the mobs and disarm the entire pull, which can be catastrophic.             
-There is a way to heal the tank without stealing aggro: using the "Calm" potion. By activating Calm, you become invisible to monsters, allowing you to heal the tank without being detected and without disarming the pull. After using Calm, you can cast "Grave Guard Helmet".

*Healer Skills and Strategies
 ◦Use of skills:
▪Throw a Q or EQ when the tank ‘hits a Q’ on bugs.
▪Throw a W when the tank does a large pull or smaller pull.
▪Use the ‘guardatumba helmet’ for powerful heals.
▪ ‘Druid's Habit’ is useful for granting mana to the party and yourself.                            ▪ Healer's Passive: After four skills, buff your heals by 20%.                                                    ▪ If you can be close to your other allies (DPS, etc.) when you cast your real jacket even better so it takes advantage of the 50% CD reduction.     
Combo: Jacket + Helmet + W + Q + E (or the other way around if you want the latter two) and keep spaming the first skill as the more you apply them the more your healing increases by ‘Q’.

title: Warbow Kite/Catch *MOCHA* Solo Content
author: Mochamille
description:
Want to rack up kills without ever breaking the bank? This is my most consistent 1 v X build!

Warbow is first and foremost a kiter, so following are some flex options to know how to fight who:

*To kite*:
- Remember that when you're playing warbow, you're at your highest dps when you're at range. maintain range from melee weapons by swapping Ray of light to frost shot. Use your frostshot reactively to jump away from weapons looking to dive you. Especially with melee opponents, dance around them at the end of your Q range. Multishot with its slow makes landing your Magic Arrows (E) very consistent.

- If someone starts running in a close fight, go back to basics. You're a kiter *FIRST*. It is melee players' jobs to catch you, not for you to catch them. Keep them in vision so you can deny any remounts, but dont even get close enough for melees to re-engage, you'll lose every close fight.

- Assassin jacket is a MITIGATION tool first. Brawlers with Mercenary jacket or Stalker Jacket (and similar options) will try to pull you into their DPS windows when they can punch back. Deny their healing or damage by simply going invisible and walking away- very rarely will you have to play as though you get a damage boost from your chest piece. In fights where damage is inevitable and reflectable, swap to infernal shield, this way when trading blows with Spears and other flexible gearsets, you will never be taking free hits.

**NOTE**: If you're doing content where youre expecting to trade hits, swap healing pots. Otherwise if you find yourself having to chase, use Poison pots for the slow and guaranteed damage.

*To Catch*
- Warbow is comfiest at range, to maintain range against other ranged matchups, you will want to keep ray of light, and instead swap to Deadly shot over Multishot. instead of using your Magic Arrow (E) around frost shot and multishots slow, you will instead use your ray of light to guarantee hits.

- Same ideas apply with the second kiting portion of this written guide: if you are getting kited by another kiter, it is safer to take the reset than to chase if the fight is close. You are in more control when someone else is chasing.

- Use the kiting portion of this guide if you're holding to more nefarious ganking activities first. Gatherers remount on a dime, so the moment you see one, the best way to catch them is to swap wanderlust on your boots, and stealth just out of vision range to get closer. use Ray of Light to catch them and despawn mounts, otherwise you will have trouble catching up again. wanderlust early after a gatherer sprints and ensure you dont get purged. Your stacking movement speed and overwhelming range will keep you close enough to make sure there are few opportunities to remount.

*Conclusion*
This build is extremely consistent and with mastery will allow you to take on far stronger opponents with ease if played perfect.

This is by no means an uncommon build, but knowing your limitations will make even the most confident players at minimum struggle heavily to kill you.

Good luck, and happy ganking!

title: Bloodletter Brawler -*MOCHA*- Solo Content
author: Mochamille
description:
*Combat Breakdown*

Flex abilities:
Sunder Armor / Forbidden stab:
Swap these particularly to deal with low mobility healers and brawlers. *DO NOT* swap off dash if its a matchup you need to do more than sprint to keep up with a run.

Swift Cut:
if you need to be particularly sticky (think warbow or certain brawling gloves), swap to swift cut to keep up. Especially potent against weapons without consistent interrupts.

*General tips and Tricks*
This is a brawling build. you always want to be hitting the enemy, so play to mitigate counterplay on you maintaining pressure.

What this looks like:
- hunter hood is almost always cause to pop Gigantify pots, if you're on top of your target and they use a reflect, counter it with gig pot to keep hitting them without consequence.

- if mercenary jacket sees value, you'll almost always lose the fight. Pop everlasting spirit to deny any healing if you see your opponent looking to use it to keep brawling.

- chain slash has really strong invulnerability frames. Use this ability to counter telegraphed high-damaging abilities (Think Claymore E, Warbow E and the like). denying large amounts of damage will make even uneven IP matchups far easier to play.

- since you're not kiting with this build, *DO NOT* use hunter hood to mitigate damage. Use it to even out guaranteed hits. If you don't have the CDs to react properly to something, or space to move out of the way, pop the reflect so that you don't take any free damage.

Conclusion:
This build is cheap but effective, even with minimal spec. The challenge is knowing what to mitigate and hitting matchup knowledge effectively. The more familiar you are with an opponent's weapon, the higher your win rate will get using this build.

Enjoy!

author: ThaiSweetChili
description:
Budget Curse Staff build, you can swap the Skull for any of the Curse staffs depending on your budget. The Demonic staff is the only one I would not recommend, as it fears all the mobs and could ruin the lure. 

With this build you will apply a lot of strong DoT and have great AoE.

Once the tank has clumped the mobs, throw your (Q), then throw (E), then use (W).

Hood & Boots are for Cooldown regen, so you can get your (E) back ASAP.

title: Light Crossbow Budget DPS Group Fame Farm Build
author: ThaiSweetChili
description:
This is a very high DPS build, and it doesn't cost a lot either. 

All you have to do is spam your spells in order to stack your (R) on your robe and get the reset on your (Q). Be mindful of the little icon under your name/healthbar. When it reaches 3, use your (Q) and then you can cast again for a double (Q). Your robe/helmet/boots skills also count towards stacking the (R) and the (Q) reset. 

You can take the new crossbow (W) for resistance shred, or Caltrops (W) for movespeed and quicker spell spamming.

Take Lymhurst cape if you use mage's cowl for the fire, but honestly Caerleon cape is a nice boost to your dps and then you take Druid Cowl for energy regen.

Mistcaller has nice cooldown, but Cryptcandle has higher dps overall. Depends on your budget.

title: Spirit Hunter Budget Support DPS PvE Group Fame Farm
author: ThaiSweetChili
description:
This is a cheap build focused entirely around using the (E) to shred resistances of the mobs and apply DoT.

Wait for your tank to lure the mobs and clump them. Throw your (E), then use (W). 

Channel your hood & pop boots to get your cooldowns back. 

Might need a couple of (Q) before you can (E) + (W) again.

You can swap the robe out for something like a Royal Jacket if you got the money, it's nice, but not needed. 

If you take Druid Cowl for your team, you can use Thetford cape for more DPS.

title: Nature Staff Budget Healer PvE Group Fame Farm
author: ThaiSweetChili
description:
The nature staff is such a flexible weapon, there are so many options to choose from for weapon skills,  helmet and boots. I chose these ones as beginner friendly, budget secondary healer options. If you don't need as much healing you can swap to Thorns on (Q). You can use pretty much any Nature Staff you want for this build. 

As secondary healer, you will be keeping the DPS and the healer alive, as well as helping keep the tank healthy if needed.

Use your flowers (Q), place them near your DPS, they can walk on them when needed. You can use the first single target lock on (Q) but then you will need to swap to rejuvenating breeze on (W).

Your Cleanse Heal (W) can be clutch if you need to get someone out of a sticky situation. It removes all CC and gives a burst heal. You can swap it to one of the other options if it's not needed. 

Helmet, Guardian gives everyone a shield, really nice, also removes DoT. If not take Graveguard for another burst heal.

You could take cleric helmet for the Ice Block to turn invincible if in trouble, but I think Guardian brings more value to the group.

Knight boots, for the shield dash, it's another shield and helps reposition. Or you can use Cloth Sandals for energy sprint and stronger heal.

Lymhurst cape for energy.

Omelette for CD.

Calming Potion for get out of jail free card in a bad lure.

title: 1H Mace Budget Tank PvE Group Fame Farm
author: ThaiSweetChili
description:
This is the Budget Version of the Incubus Mace build. Similar playstyle, just cheaper because of the weapon and shield. Tbh the 1H Mace is really nice, the stun is big. But the shrink on Incubus is stronger. 2H Mace with the silence on (E) also works, but then you are less beefy without a shield. 

Playstyle Tips 

- Pop Boots followed by Air Compressor (W), run through the mobs, try to pull as many as you can. 

- Slam the mobs with your Deep Leap jump stun (E).

- Pop Helmet / Armour. Use Threatening Smash (Q) on the mobs while the team gets in position. 

- Keep using (Q) when available. 

Alternatives/Situational

- Soldier Helmet for the block if you are fighting strong enemies and don't want to dodge the skill to make it easier for your healer and team.

- Hunter Hood for when you are fighting weaker enemies, they take so much damage from their own attacks, makes it a lot quicker if you can tank it.

- You can take Heavy Boots if you want to be tankier, or you can take any other Leather boot and take the Cooldown Sprint.

- Hunter boots do give you a big burst of speed which makes it easier to catch the mobs in a (W). But its your choice.

- Potion only needed for when you are in trouble or there is lots of CC. (Also to escape ganker  CC if in PvP Zone)

- Sandwhich for HP  boost, making tanking easier.

This is budget build for beginner content, so no need to take crazy expensive food or change the pieces.

title: Holy Staff Budget Healer PvE Group Fame Farm
author: ThaiSweetChili
description:
You can use any 1H Holy Staff with this build. The first one is the cheapest. You can use any 2H Holy Staff too but you will lose the bonuses that come with the Off Hand. 

As a holy staff healer, you'll be the primary, frontline healer, meaning your focus is on keeping the tank alive. Don't worry so much about the rest of the team, if the tank dies, everyone dies. 

If there are two healers, then you one of you will be the secondary, backline healer, who can heal the other team members and help with healing the tank if needed. 

Whether primary or secondary healer, NEVER let the tank die. 

Mistcaller usually lower price than Celestial Censer, plus I prefer the Cooldown. But Censer offers way bigger heals at the cost of defence.

Druid Cowl = Infinite Energy. Graveguard Helmet has a clutch burst heal if needed. Tbh this depends on whether we have another Druid Cowl or not in the team. 

Cleric Robe is budget friendly, Royal Robe if you're ballin'.

Knight Boots have a nice Shield Dash, to reposition and save. If not just take Cloth Sandals for more heal power and energy.

Lymhurst cape is the budget option. Caerleon for instant double (Q), I don't think it's necessary but it can be nice.

Energy Potion or Calming, situational.  

Omelette for the juicy cooldown.

title: Chill Howl Budget DPS PvE Group Fame Farm
author: ThaiSweetChili
description:
Crazy high DPS build. You can use Permafrost Prism instead of Chillhowl for bigger CC + DPS on (E) but you actually lose DPS cos of the offhand bonuses you get with 1H Chillhowl, Permafrost is also quite a bit more pricey.

You can use Glacial, Great Frost, maybe even 1H Frost too. The DPS comes from the (Q) spam anyway. 
 
Scholar Robe + Lyhmurst Cape if you want cheaper build. But Morgana Cape + Druid Cowl + Druid Robe is Better.

If you are using Scholars Robe, you must pop your (R) before you start spamming (Q). Always stand in your (W). It gives cooldown and damage. If you are using Morgana Cape you get the speed casting for free after (E) Cast. 

If using Druid Robe, pop (R) before you start spamming your (Q).

Be careful who you cast your (E) on. No one else can damage or heal the person/mob trapped in there. 

Mistcaller if you want extra cheap, if not Cryptcandle for more DPS. 

Omelette better for this weapon, but stew an option.

Calming potion if team gets in bad lure with mobs.

title: Fire Staff Budget DPS PvE Group Fame Farm
author: ThaiSweetChili
description:
Cheapest Fire Staff Build with plenty of AOE.  Blazing Staff + Maybe the Pheonix Orb will deal more damage or have better (E) but this build packs a big punch for a low price.

On Staff you can take any (W) really, but I think Raging Flare or Flame Blast are best. 

Druid Cowl for infinite energy. Assassin Hood for low cooldown.

Druid Robe for crazy damage, Cleric if Druid too pricey.

Cloth Sandals for more DPS and Energy. Leather Shoes for Cooldown.

Thetford Cape for more DPS , ( You will weave in some autos when your skills are on cooldown )

Lymhurst Cape if you took Assassin Hood. 

Stew or Omelette. Stew is more DPS but Omelette lowers your cooldowns so you can spam more. I'm not sure which is better, up to you. 

Calming Potion for if anyone gets in trouble with the lure. Just don't use on the tank.

title: Druidic Staff Solo Pve Open World
author: Weaszy
description:
Build and infos provided by the legend u/Folksvaletti !

Super cheap build that you can kill even the strongest mobs with just 4.3 or even 4.2 if u have enough specs or know how to fight most of the mobs...

Weapon Skills:

Q2 Thorn Growth/Vines

W3 Protection of Nature (Increase healing received by 35%)

First Passive, Adrenaline Driven... (Increase healing cast by 20%)

You want to keep casting your first skill under the enemy mob, and then hit them with auto attacks to proc the extra dmg that your dmg skill does when using auto attacks to follow up.

When you get damaged for 1 bar of your hp, wait until you get your 4 cast healing buff from your weapon passive, then cast your second skill (Protection of nature) on yourself and immediately after that, also cast your main weapon skill on yourself, your E... It will give a massive heal since you get +35% from your W and +20% healing from your passive.

If someone tries to gank you, first of all, keep calm! If you can’t mount up in time, use your assassin jacket to disaggro mobs and get as far away from them (player) as possible, while not leaving the invisibility circle. Then IN THAT ORDER, use your boots and drink your potion and run to any gate or portal which u can enter instantly to get a shield after going through and then being able to mount up without risks of them cancelling it... After mounted, try to get to safety, Smuggler Dens, another roads of avalon maybe, etc... Remember to use your boots before the potion, otherwise you’ll go invis and come out when you pop the boots xd

Since you come out of invis if you take damage, remember to keep your guardian helmet for clearing DOTs, damages over time like fire, bleed, curse stacks... Soo you can drink the potion without taking damage from them and losing the invisibility instantly.

It uses an Assassin Hood to reduce cooldown times substantially, which makes picking off enemies even faster - The Boltcaster's spells are selected for maximum one-shotting capability, the Deathward Climax does wonders - The Robe of Purity has many uses, you can use it to keep melee attackers away while you chew them apart with Deathward Climax or you can use it to keep people away from you while using your Assasin Hood. title: [1H Nature] [Open World] Solo Roam
author: Crusang
description:
This build is simple, affordable, and easy to grasp for its purpose. While it lacks mobility and isn’t meant for 1vX or picking up PvP fights at will, it has got the power to clear camps/enchanted mobs quickly enough to hop onto the next batch of them.

Full mage set might sound like a meme or a role-play choice, but it’s actually very effective for what this build aims to do.

We're picking up mage cowl for added DPS in our rotation for faster clears, our mage robe has the highest damage % of all chest pieces at the cheapest price and also its ability acts as a purge/resistance potion. Shoe slot is flexible, we're only after energetic sprint here, so any sandal works here.

Set can sway more into PvP by swapping to Guardian helmet, Cleric robe and Soldier boots, as both the helmet and robe offer a defensive, letting you mount when taking damage, or tank massive incoming damage, while retaining enough damage to continue clearing objectives decently enough. 
You can even swap Cleric robe with Mercenary jacket for the classic set, but that sways too much off the focus point of this build.

Muisak for the added heal/damage bonus, with no negative as using the 2nd passive on nature staff gets us mana on autos. Can swap with torch for faster autos and more cooldown reduction, depending on your gameplay.
Reason we're not selecting crypt candle is due to it lowering our defenses, making us even squishier. The blueflame torch currently is too expensive therefore making it moot to even recommend.
Facebreaker also works for additional defense while keeping some damage boost, so keep that in mind.

Thetford cape for added damage, can susbtitute with a normal cape for an even cheaper price. Martlock cape can be used if you're willing to pick up more PvP fights.

Potions are a choice, resist for tankiness, poison for PvE focus, invisibility to try and escape players, gigantify if you want to fight back, or even hellfire potions for a one-shot type of build (requires royal helmet as well).

Food is a choice as well, I pick beef stew for the additional damage on Q/W/E, can pick the avalonian version for HP regen between fights/resets, or can do T7 omelette for lower cooldowns and cast times.

title: Infinity Blade small-scale pvp/ pve..?
author: Canoob
description:
WARNING: 
The infinity Blade is "Off-Meta" because of it's nerfs, it also requires a certain learning curves for it to be good. 

Tip 1: Do not use all your skills mindlessly, in a pve and especially pvp situation, you WILL NOT be able to continue the fight because of the cool downs, like any other build. You need to be smart with the skills you use.

Tip 2: You will NOT deal huge damage like the fire mentor staff, instead, you HAVE to spec your weapon up. Having food that increases damage can also help, but speccing your weapon to 100 is a MUST to deal actual damage. Please look on YouTube before purchasing this build, it is normal to feel underwhelmed at a <100 spec gear.

Tip 3: DO NOT go to lethal zones with this if you aren't going to be smart. You will be targeted since the Infinity Blade is a crystal weapon, and crystal weapons are sought after because of their prices.

Faction warfare: 

ALWAYS stay near your group, NEVER go alone, I mean it.

NEVER stay near to "spectate" fights, I've done it, tried it, it went horrible very fast. You cannot escape if you get pulled in.

DO NOT open the faction chest when the objective is completed instantly, there is a 35-45% (assumption based on my runs) to get bombed by the meteor skill from the fire staff that I mentionned earlier, you WILL get one shotted. Instead, wait 5-10 seconds at a safe distance from the chest, then pop your head skill and open the chest. Use a gigantify potion if you want to be "extra" safe.

Blackzone:

I haven't done much BZ, but what I can tell you, is that people are bloodthirsty there. 
NEVER go with this type of gear if you ARE NOT EXPERIENCED.
Only advanced players should go with this gear. If you are a newbie and go in BZ with this gear, you WILL get frustrated. I can guarantee it. RedZone is an exception because of the amount of players you can be with that are from your faction.

Reminder:

Those are "TIPS", I don't guarantee that you will be safe in RZ/BZ with this type of gear, those are only precautions.

You will be fine if you stick to YZ content, Orange zone is also an option.

title: Ava Road 7 player Tombhammer
author: Kat
description:
Ava road small scale team comp around oneshotting one enemy at a time and disengaging 
Tombhammer's job is to stun any isolated target and call for their team to oneshot them, if they have any kind of cleanse, since Tombhammer's CD is just 15 seconds, you can fake engage using your cds and make them waste cleanse so the next time you have your E they wont have cleanse, thats the big reason why Tombhammer is the choice instead of other hammers
You combine E stun -> W knockup -> boots knock up to CC them for your team to drop damage, pop your Helmet stun and your chest silence to disengage safely after that

Swap your W to Inertia Ring if going against a full pressure comp
Swap to Hellion hood if you are 6 players instead of 7, 7th slot is for mace so you wont have Helion hood for peel/disengage
Run Acid when you have a rotcaller and hellfire when you dont

author: Kyro
description:
Off Tank - Hand of Justice (HOJ)

Účel buildu: Hlavní engage a shotcalling. Facecheckuješ nebezpečné zóny, zjišťuješ pozici nepřítele a hlásíš organizaci a pohyb vlastní skupiny.

Jak hrát:

Pohyb: Jdeš v čele formace, určuješ směr a připravuješ engage.

Engage: Použij Boty (Stalker Shoes) ke skoku přímo doprostřed nepřátelského davu

Okamžitě aktivuj E, čímž se s kladivem roztočíš a stáhneš všechny lidi kolem sebe na jednu hromadu

Judicator Armor (Main): Zapni armor pro zvýšení obrany a příjmu léčení v centru dění, abys přežil focus
