description:
Stopper - 1H Mace 

Účel buildu: Defenzivní "Counter-Engage" tank. Tvou prioritou není útočit jako první, ale hlídat vlastní backline (healery a DPS) a překazit enemy engage.

Jak hrát:

Pozice: Drž se staženější mezi vlastními healery a frontlinou. Nechoď příliš dopředu.

Reakce: Jakmile nepřítel zahájí engage (nebo vidíš, že se blíží), aktivuj Hunter Shoes (pro delší trvání CC) a skoč mezi hlavní enemy dps pro přerušení jejich rotace.

Guardian Armor: Ihned po dopadu aktivuj R (Enfeeble Aura). Tím zpomalíš nepřátele kolem sebe a výrazně snížíš jejich poškození, čímž zachráníš svůj tým před bombou

title: Broadsword Total Ownage
author: MightPolaris
description:
The Broadsword build using Hunter Hood, Mercenary Jacket, Scholar Sandals, Facebreaker or Sarcophagus Shield, Martlock Cape, Baked Porgfish, and Healing or Gigantify Potions is a completely off-meta setup, but extremely effective in honest duels where the fight is decided by timing, mechanics, and defensive precision.

⚔️ Core Concept
This build focuses on winning 1v1 fights through:
Consistent damage from Broadsword stacks

Interrupting key enemy abilities with your E

High sustain through the Mercenary Jacket

Damage reflection with Hunter Hood

The playstyle is straightforward: trading head-on, using your defensives at the perfect moment — usually in reaction to the enemy’s major burst skill.

🛡️ Gear Breakdown
• Broadsword
Your E is your strongest tool:

Interrupts enemy abilities
Deals burst damage
Grants movement speed

Lets you stick to your target and stop their combo

IMPORTANT:
You should always try to use your E with maximum passive stacks (3 stacks).
This gives:

Maximum damage
Maximum mobility
Maximum fight pressure

However:
If you need to interrupt a critical enemy ability, you should absolutely use your E even without max stacks. Stopping enemy burst is more valuable than saving stacks.

• Shield (Facebreaker or Sarcophagus)

Facebreaker: more aggressive and pressure-focused.
Sarcophagus: more defensive and stable for long fights.

Choose based on your preferred style.

• Hunter Hood
Your reflect tool.
Activate when your opponent:

Commits to burst
Uses rapid DPS combos
Has no way to disengage

They will damage themselves heavily, forcing them to back off or die outright.

• Mercenary Jacket
The heart of your sustain.
Provides massive healing with your fast Broadsword autos.
Best used after you interrupt the enemy’s burst or when you have clear uptime to hit.
Turns your off-meta setup into a real off-tank duelist.

• Scholar Sandals
Maintain your mana and let you reposition when needed.
Use the active to:

Recover energy
Avoid burst
Reset spacing during trades

• Martlock Cape
Your emergency defense.
It activates on low HP, helping you survive all-ins and turn close fights around.

🍗 Consumables
• Baked Porgfish
Increases damage and max HP, perfect for straight-up trading.
• Healing or Gigantify Potion
Healing Pot: most consistent sustain.
Gigantify: great against high burst; increases HP and mitigates kill pressure.

🧠 How to Play (Step-by-Step)
1. Build up your Broadsword stacks (Q) before committing.
Stacks increase your E damage and movement speed.
2. Aim to use your E with 3 stacks.
This gives the highest pressure and best engagement.
3. Blow your E early only if you must INTERRUPT a key enemy ability.
Stopping their combo is often more important than maximizing your damage.
4. After winning the trade with your E, activate Mercenary Jacket.
You need to be hitting the enemy to gain full healing value.
5. Use Hunter Hood during the enemy’s burst window.
Make them hit themselves and punish bad timing.
6. Manage energy with Scholar Sandals.
Without mana, this build collapses.
7. Let Martlock Cape save you in the final moments.
Gives you a second wind to finish the fight.

title: Fallen but Risen Holy(Fame Farm Fallen Build Static Yellow/Blue Zone)
author: Kumalatte
description: Use Graveguard as emergency heal when all healing skills are cd. before dropping E, use Q first and then drop E and another Q after when tank does a big clump. Always use W when tank is 50% hp or less to avoid overhealing(this is a healing lost which is a cooldown cost too that may cause the tank to die when you use heal too early). Using skills frequently also cost your mana to drain fast, so only heals when you have to and practice putting Q and E to heal more numbers than healing one. It is also to keep yourself alive, so heal after the clump but not before or else you'll take the mobs aggro causing the pull to be a mess and sometimes your own death. Remember that if you die as a healer, everyone may die as well.

title: Earthrune Staff ZvZ Clump Tank
author: Zeyrn
description:
A clump tank with the ability to create and hold large clumps by itself
#### How to play

- When the engage is called, use your D and boots to rush forward, W to form the beginning of a clump and proc the cast speed passive, Shapeshift then W the best clump possible
- Use your defensive on allies under engages (R) or place preemptively on chokes and bridges
- Use your Q to gain stacks and protect allies against brawlers

#### Alternative equipement

- Demon armor or Knight armor can be used depending on the composition requirement and shotcaller preference.

- Several blink, dash and jump alternative are available for more unpredictable approach : Judicator boots, Royal Shoes, Stalker shoes and Cleric sandals

- Trading the large speed boost for a more secured engage with the Graveguard boots or the boots of Valour is also an option

title: 1H Dagger Cheap Roaming Build
author: Zancrew
description:
## Overall  

This is a really good build for **roaming**.  
Its **low cost** and **versatility** make it powerful against **both mobs and players**.  
  
With this build, you can use the S.A.F.E Portal to make **several million silver** in a single hour if you're lucky enough.  

---

### Build  

Before showcasing the build, keep in mind that you can choose the tier based on your budget.  
  
This is a low-cost build: as of mid-July 2025, T4.2 costs around 150k and T5.2 about 400k (European prices).  
  
With that said, let’s take a look at what this build is made of 👇  

#### Weapons

The **Dagger** ![Dagger](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/item/T8_MAIN_DAGGER.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) paired with the **Torch** ![Torch](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/item/T8_OFF_TORCH.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) makes you formidable against melee opponents.  

Your spells **Deadly Swipe** ![Deadly Swipe](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/spell/QDASH.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) and **Chain Slash** ![Chain Slash](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/spell/CHAINDASH.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) both deal a lot of AoE damage, which is great against packs of mobs.  

**Bloodthirsty Blade** ![Bloodthirsty Blade](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/spell/BLOODTHIRSTYBLADE.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) deals a lot of damage and provides great sustain, especially when combined with your armor spell **Haste** ![Haste](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/spell/HASTE.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50).  

#### Armor  

The **Assassin Hood** ![Assassin Hood](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/item/T8_HEAD_LEATHER_SET3.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) and **Mage Sandals** ![Mage Sandals](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/item/T8_SHOES_CLOTH_SET3.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) are purely utility items, allowing you to combo more often and never run out of energy.  

The **Hunter Jacket** ![Hunter Jacket](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/item/T8_ARMOR_LEATHER_SET2.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) is the **key item** of the build, as its **Haste** ![Haste](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/spell/HASTE.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) boosts your attack speed by 60% and damage by 20% for 8 seconds. Its cooldown is 30 seconds, but your torch and the helmet ability **Meditation** ![Meditation](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/spell/SUMMONER_CD_REDUCTION.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) will reduce it significantly.

#### Accessories  

I suggest you take a bag sized for your **looting goals**. If you plan to stay in the Black Zone for two hours without returning home, you might want to bring a higher-tier bag. Eitherway, a T4.0 or T4.1 bag is enough.  

If you're rich enough, you can consider using a **Thetford Cape** ![Thetford Cape](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/item/T8_CAPEITEM_FW_THETFORD.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50). This is the best cape for this build, as it’s effective against both mobs and players.  

Otherwise, you can go for an **Avalonian Cape** ![Avalonian Cape](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/item/T8_CAPEITEM_AVALON.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50), which is also great and currently cheaper.  

*If you want to go for a cheap build, you can also take no cape at all.*  

---

### Combo

I suggest you play differently depending on whether you're in PvE or PvP 👇  

#### PvE Combo 

Against mobs, I suggest you do the following: `W > Q > R > E`.  
Once everything is on cooldown, press `F > D` and repeat the sequence.  

This will obliterate the mobs you're fighting, as they can't kite you.  

#### PvP Combo

Against players, you will need to replace your W ability **Chain Slash** ![Chain Slash](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/spell/CHAINDASH.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) with **Shadow Edge** ![Shadow Edge](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/spell/SKILLSHOT_TELEPORT.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50).  
This is essential, as the build struggles against kiting players.  

The combo remains the same: `W > Q > R > E`.  
Once everything is on cooldown, press `F > D` and repeat the sequence.  

*Important: you should try to get close to your opponent without using your `W`, to prevent them from kiting or escaping you. The Invisibility Potion can be a great way to achieve this.*  

---

### Consumables  

If you're planning to focus on PvE only, then the **Invisibility Potion** ![Invisibility Potion](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/item/T8_POTION_CLEANSE.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) paired with **Cabbage Soup** ![Cabbage Soup](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/item/T5_MEAL_SOUP.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) will be your best choice, as it's safe and reduces your chances of dying.  

If you're planning on taking PvP fights as well, then you should use a **Major Healing Potion** ![Major Healing Potion](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/item/T6_POTION_HEAL.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) paired with **Deadwater Eel Stew** ![Deadwater Eel Stew](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/item/T8_MEAL_STEW_FISH.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50), as these are more effective in PvP battles.  

---

### Mount  

For a really cheap build, the **Journeyman’s Riding Horse** might be the best option.  
For a more expensive version of the build, you’ll want to use an **Expert’s Armored Horse** to avoid getting dismounted too quickly and to escape ganks more easily.  

---

Thank you for reading until the end! If you enjoyed this build, feel free to give it an upvote! 😃

title: Bear Paws Solo Gank & Brawl Build
author: Zancrew
description:
*Be aware that this build has a steep learning curve and requires a lot of practice!*

## Recommended Build

This build is highly effective for **solo ganking**, offering both high burst damage and great mobility.  
It’s ideal for taking down less well-equipped players within seconds.  

Ambush ![Ambush](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/spell/AMBUSH.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50), Invisibility Potion ![Invisibility Potion](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/item/T8_POTION_CLEANSE.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) and Undead Cape ![Undead Cape](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/item/T8_CAPEITEM_UNDEAD.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) provide **7, 7, and 6 seconds of invisibility**, respectively.  

This makes them perfect for sneaky engagements or escaping from unfavorable fights.  

Good to know: you can still deal damage while the **Undead Cape** ![Undead Cape](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/item/T8_CAPEITEM_UNDEAD.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) passive **Vanisher** ![Vanisher](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/spell/PASSIVE_REDUCED_ENERGYCOST.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) is active. However, all your damage (and healing) is reduced by 50% during the effect. This still gives you a significant advantage in combat.  

---

### Spells and Combo

The combo sequence is: `F > W > E > Q > Q > Q`  

Begin your gank by activating **Defenseless Rush** ![Defenseless Rush](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/spell/GLASS_MOVESPEED.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) to quickly close the gap to your target.   

Once you’re in range, use **Adrenaline Boost** ![Adrenaline Boost](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/spell/AXEBOOST.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) to amplify your damage output.  

Next, engage with **Razor Cut** ![Razor Cut](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/spell/DUALAXE_CRAWLER.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) to dash directly into melee range.  

Finish with a triple **Rending Rage** ![Rending Rage](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/spell/RENDINGCOMBO.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) combo to secure the kill.  

Use **Purge** ![Purge](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/spell/PURGE_HELMET.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) to cancel your opponent’s speed boost buff and prevent their escape.  

---

### Consumables

The recommended consumables are perfect for the Black Zone: the Invisibility Potion’s ![Invisibility Potion](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/item/T8_POTION_CLEANSE.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) versatility and the Cabbage Soup’s ![Cabbage Soup](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/item/T5_MEAL_SOUP.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) passive healing lower your chances of dying and make fights much safer to take.  

However, swapping to a Major Poison Potion ![Major Poison Potion](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/item/T8_POTION_COOLDOWN.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) combined with a Deadwater Eel Stew ![Deadwater Eel Stew](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/item/T8_MEAL_STEW_FISH.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) makes your build far more aggressive. The choice is yours!

---

## Alternative Build

You can alternatively adopt a more brawler-style play by replacing the jacket and the cape.  

The Mercenary Jacket ![Mercenary Jacket](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/item/T8_ARMOR_LEATHER_SET1.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) is a great choice against melee opponents, as its **Bloodlust** ![Bloodlust](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/spell/BLOODLUST.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) provides self-healing for up to 7 hits, greatly increasing your sustain and extending your time in fights.  

The Thetford Cape ![Thetford Cape](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/item/T8_CAPEITEM_FW_THETFORD.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) is another strong option, as its **Chain Lightning** ![Chain Lightning](https://render.albiononline.com/v1/spell/PASSIVE_REDUCED_ENERGYCOST.png?count=1&quality=1&size=50) boosts your overall DPS by dealing extra magic damage to up to 4 targets, making it especially effective in fights against multiple opponents.

title: Basic Battleaxe Build
author: JerBear84
description:
I've played this build a ton and seen it over and over in YouTube as well as in opponents in CD. 

It's just what a new player should look for: Tons of sustain with Mercendary Jacket, Soldier Boots, and Battleaxe E, a safe and reliable defensive to ensure you can always mount up in the Guardian Helmet, and steady damage from the Axe and Torch. 

Martlock cape is as basic as it gets, offering more life when you need it with zero effort. If you can't afford it (it's the only pricy thing in the build) a beach towel plain cape will work fine too.

The only problem with this build is you'll have to switch out the items once they reach 100 😅

More notes:

- When roaming in lethal zones keep invisibility potion handy in case you need to get away, but the poison is a good swap for tough bosses. When I expect a PVP fight, I equip a health potion. 

- Rending Rage (Q3) takes forever to unlock, use Q2 until you get there

- Soldier boots can be any plate boots, though the most likely swap from Rejuvenating Sprint (all plate boots) is Wanderlust, so you might as well have Soldier boots leveled up first. 

- Of course when it comes to Battleaxe E, avoid using the second healing throw unless you really need the health, or it will for sure kill the enemy. The extra cooldown time of using the second throw isn't worth it just for damage in the middle of a fight.

title: Lightcaller clap RDPS
author: mystisksang
description:
Optimal combo:
Obsessive Burst - 2x Pulse Shock - Distortion - Transform - Judgement - Piercing Light

This combo should give you 5 stacks of Obsessive Burst before Judgement for a 30% damage boost. if you cannot get full combo off due to cape cd, robe cd, etc. then try to transform with at least 3 stacks so you can use Judgement + Piercing Light.

title: Energy Shaper clap RDPS
author: mystisksang
description: After stacking passive using Explosive bolt and Caltrops, use Defenseless Rush and drop your E on the clump. Cleric Robe and Stalker Shoes should be used defensively (if applicable).

title: Siegebow clap RDPS
author: mystisksang
description:
Try to stack your passive using Explosive Bolt and Caltrops, then drop your E on clump after using Hyper Focus on Feyscale Hat. This will make your cast uninterruptible.
Assassin Hood is also a viable option, so it is up to personal preference.

title: Mistpiercer clap RDPS
author: mystisksang
description: On your caller's clump, pop Explosive Arrows, Speed Caster, and Royal Sandals (if applicable), then spam out all E casts on the clump. Otherwise, poke at enemies using Deadly Shot for the damage and bit of extra pierce.

title: Longbow clap RDPS
author: mystisksang
description: Primary job is to wait for engages and pop Explosive Arrows before using Rain of Arrows on the clump. Spam Deadly Shot off-cooldown to get the bonus pierce on enemies and use Cleric/Feyscale robe defensively.

title: Brimstone Staff bomb RDPS
author: mystisksang
description: As enemies are clumped by your caller, pop Speed Caster and immediately follow up with your E. Using feyscale hat is optional and generally unnecessary but is up to preference. Use Burning Field on clump after E cast ends and continue using it to poke at enemies. Use Wall of Flames defensively to stall enemy engages while waiting for your own engage.

title: Blazing Staff clap RDPS
author: mystisksang
description: Once enemies are clumped by your caller, pop Speed Caster and drop Flame Tornado on the clump, followed by Burning Field. Continue using Burning Field to poke at enemies and use Fire Wall to stall for time as we kite back and wait for next clap. If possible, try to time your clap with Furious proc, but it is not necessary.

title: Wildfire Staff clap RDPS
author: mystisksang
description: Drop Magma Sphere on clumps and poke using Burning Field. You will most likely be on Fire Wall, so use it to stop engages and to stall while waiting for next clap.

title: Permafrost Prism CC RDPS
author: mystisksang
description: Before a clump, pop your Scholar Robe and use Ice Crystal on the clump as fast as you can. After dropping Ice Crystal, spam Ice Shard for the duration of the Morgana Cape and Scholar Robe for lots of aoe damage. Save Frost Nova for self-peel, may be used to get closer to use E on clump if you are not in a good position to hit it.

title: Dawnsong heal cut RDPS
author: mystisksang
description: Your job is to drop your Flaming Phoenix on clumps and poke with Burning Field. This provides a 40% heal cut on the clump along with a significant amount of burst damage.

title: Damnation Staff pierce RDPS
author: mystisksang
description: use Feyscale Hat and Scholar Robe before casting E on a clump to make the cast uninterruptible and faster. (Feyscale Hat optional and swappable for Assassin Hood). Make sure to time E well to hit pierce before primary dps. Poke with Cursed Tar and use Armor Piercer shortly after your E finishes casting for even MORE pierce.

title: Daybreaker purge MDPS/support
author: mystisksang
description:
Primary job is to drop purge on clumps, along with an Impaler. Aside from this, just brawling and poking with Lunging Strike can be beneficial if you are able to. Before using Breakthrough, pop Cultist Sandals so that you can also apply an extra pierce on top of the purge.

As a Daybreaker, you also have a lot more build diversity as a higher utility MDPS, so Judicator/Knight/Duskweaver armor can all work. You can push enemies into your team by using your E into them to purge defensives like knight helm and using Duskweaver Boots to push them into your team, an amazing way to catch enemies off guard (assuming your caller approves).

title: Bloodletter execute MDPS
author: mystisksang
description:
Your job as a bloodletter is to execute enemies on a clump after your primary damage has dropped, but fast enough that they do not have time to get away, so timing is crucial. Use Dash to get in and execute using Mortal Agony and Lunging Stabs. Use Stalker shoes to get out when needed.

Do not forget to use Jacket of Tenacity and to full stack using Assassin Spirit before executing.

title: Infernal Scythe execute MDPS
author: mystisksang
description: Primary job is to place stacks on enemies and wait for clap. When enemies are clumped, use Battle Rush to dash into them and execute using Mortal Agony and Bloody Reap (in that order) after your primary damage has dropped.

title: Carving Sword pierce MDPS/support
author: mystisksang
description: Primary job is to stack using Iron Will and Heroic Cleave, then hit your pierce on a clump, immediately after the Permafrost. You can opt to either go Hellion Jacket for the survivability or Judicator Armor, as your damage is somewhat negligible compared to the primary MDPS.

title: Rift Glaive clap MDPS
author: mystisksang
description: Full stack with Spirit Spear and use Inner Focus + Jacket of Tenacity to stack damage buffs. Drop E on clump then run back to avoid retaliation damage.

title: Kingmaker clap/MDPS
author: mystisksang
description: Gain stacks from enemies using Q2 and Iron Will. A single Q and Iron Will should give max stacks for a clap. Watch your caller for engages and be ready to drop Majestic Smash as soon as possible. Use Jacket of Tenacity beforehand for the damage and defense bonus and Stalker Shoes defensively.

title: Spirithunter pierce MDPS
author: mystisksang
description: Primary job is to drop Corrupting Steel and Impaler on a clump as fast as possible for the pierce to affect your teammates' damage. Use Jacket of Tenacity beforehand for optimal damage buffs.

title: Realmbreaker pierce MDPS
author: mystisksang
description: Use Jacket of Tenacity before claps to buff damage. Primary damage is from Aftershock, which you can boost with Adrenaline Boost. If brawling with Hellion Jacket, you may swap to Raging Blades and Rending Spin.

title: Fists Of Avalon clap/MDPS
author: mystisksang
description: Only real job as a spiked is to hit your Purifying Combination on clumps. Q and W should be used as mobility and not for much else, unless needed to push an enemy into your team (but not out of allied damage). Use Jacket of Tenacity to increase your damage and Assassin Hood to refresh necessary cooldowns.

title: Hellfire Hands clap/MDPS
author: mystisksang
description: Primary job is to drop Infernal Boulder on clumped enemies. Q and W should be used primarily as mobility and not for much else, unless needed to push an enemy into your team (but not out of allied damage). Use Jacket of Tenacity to increase your damage and Helmet of Valor to purge enemy defensives on clumps or to cleanse yourself and allies of debuffs/cc.

title: Spiked Gauntlets clap/MDPS
author: mystisksang
description:
Only real job as a spiked is to hit your Gravitational Collapse on clumps. Q and W should be used as mobility and not for much else, unless needed to push an enemy into your team (but not out of allied damage).
Use Jacket of Tenacity to increase your damage and Helmet of Valor to purge enemy defensives on clumps or to cleanse yourself and allies of debuffs/cc.

title: Bridled Fury clap
author: mystisksang
description: Primary job is to play as a bomb/clap, do NOT brawl if at all posssible. Get 3 stacks with Assassin Spirit and full stack Royal Hood, use Hellion Shoes to go in, and use Throwing Blades and Merciless Finish to get a big burst off. Cleric Cowl and Cleric Robe should primarily be used defensively, but recommended set uses Royal Hood for extra damage.

title: Heron Spear MDPS
author: mystisksang
description: Brawl with enemies and wait for primary engage to clump enemies. Once clumped, E into W for optimal burst damage and use stalker shoes to get out. Use Hellion Jacket when needed and Scholar Cowl to regen energy when needed.

title: Oathkeepers tank support
author: mystisksang
description:
Use Blessed Aurora to apply shields to allies and give them a movement speed bonus. If in range, auto during the buff to heal nearby allies.

Guard Rune will be the most commonly-used W ability as a support, but Snare Charge is a viable option.

title: Evensong support
author: mystisksang
description: Use Magic Shock off-cooldown to silence enemies or Arcane Protection to shield allies and Motivating Cleanse to cleanse cc. Drop E on clumps to reduce healing received and damage done, as well as applying a slow. The heal cut goes up to 75%, making it really hard for them to get healed up after being clumped and bursted down.

title: Rootbound Staff support
author: mystisksang
description:
While in human form, use Adapting Matter to gain stacks and to shield allies, as well as Tether Shift to help out allies that need it (please do not troll with it in an actual fight). When you have enough shift charges, you can go into tree form and start placing Qs on groups of allies, buffing the healing they receive and healing them for a small amount.

Your W in tree form should be used defensively, as it applies a shield to allies and gives them the same effects as a Knight Helmet. This also slows enemies by 50% so can be used to peel if needed.

title: Occult Staff reset support
author: mystisksang
description:
Your primary job as an Occult is to use Motivating Cleanse when needed and use E when caller asks for it. You can also use E on your own as you get more used to group fights and start learning when to use it to help reset.

You will likely be on Royal Jacket, so you would ideally want to pop royal between claps, preferably at the end of your carpet.

title: Enigmatic Staff support
author: mystisksang
description:
Primary job is to apply shields on enemy engages and use your Motivating Cleanse on allies to prevent them from getting CC'ed too hard.

Use feyscale hat before casting E.

Feyscale swappable for Knight Helmet, but Feyscale is far better in most cases.

title: Malevolent Locus support
author: mystisksang
description:
Primary Job as a locus differs depending on what your caller prefers.
Offensive Locus: Purge enemy buffs and any debuffs/cc while attacking, allows for purge of defensive abilities on clumps.
Defensive Locus: Purge enemy buffs and debuffs/cc from team while defending. 

Can also play more flexibly between offensive and defensive when you get more experience in the role.

Use Motivating cleanse on top of your E for extra safety, but there is leeway for running Mimic depending on your experience with it.

title: 1h Arcane purge support
author: mystisksang
description:
Primary purpose is to purge and silence enemies on their engage as a stopper, or to purge defensives on a clump when necessary. Use Motivating Cleanse when necessary, can be swapped to Mimic if you are good at using it (high skill ability) and if the group has cleanses.

Plate passive can be swapped to toughness based on preference.

title: Forgebark Staff utility party healer
author: mystisksang
description:
Alternative party healer to blight staff. More complex with E usage. Use red E to root enemies and buff ally damage on claps and green E for the remainder of the duration to shield*/heal allies. Place flowers on allies to easily apply stacks and use either Rejuvenating Breeze or Cleanse Heal depending on numbers.
*Note that shield recast is fully spammable.

title: Lifecurse purge support
author: mystisksang
description: Primary purge support. Use Enfeeble Blades on clumps to purge defensives or on chokes to purge enemy engages. W can be swapped between Desecrate and Armor Piercer by caller's preference or self preference. Feel free to apply stacks with Q, but your damage will not be significant with plate armor.

title: Blight Staff party healer
author: mystisksang
description: Primary party healer when running 1 holy + 1 nature. Focus primarily on healing backline and maintaining stacks on entire party if possible. W ability can be on either Cleanse Heal or Rejuvenating Breeze depending on party size and comp. Try to place flowers on top of people so that they do not have to walk into them, preferably on clumps of allies.

title: Great Holy alternative burst healer
author: mystisksang
description: Alternative burst healer to hallowfall. As frontline healer, focus burst heals on mdps and tanks or focus on burst healing as solo healer. E can be used solely for healing or can be used defensively to peel for team.

title: Hallowfall burst healer
author: mystisksang
description: Primary focus on burst healing frontline unless you are solo healer. E should be used primarily for safety, but can situationally be used for CC/catch or healing when needed. Feyscale robe usage should consist primarily of the fire wall, but the reflect may be useful depending on situation.

title: Great Arcane stopper
author: mystisksang
description: Primary job is to full stop enemy engages with Time Freeze, as it is uncleanseable and is not affected by Displacement Immunity. This is best placed on either an engaging tank or on the primary dps so that they cannot follow up. Shield self or allies with Arcane Protection and use Motivating Cleanse on CC'ed allies.

title: Grailseeker stopper
author: mystisksang
description: Use Soul Shaker to wall off enemy engages, preferably at an angle. Rising Blow can also stall enemy engages, but can be swapped for Forceful Swing or Separator based on preference and positioning. Q can also be used to interrupt enemies, but can also be used for mobility.

title: Grovekeeper stopper
author: mystisksang
description: Use Ground Pound to interrupt enemy engages, followed by Inertia Ring and Mythical Web when necessary. Electric Discharge may also be used to stall engages slightly and buy time for other stoppers.

title: 1h Hammer stopper
author: mytisksang
description: Play inside enemies and be ready to use your E to interrupt their engages. Leering cane is necessary for bonus cc duration. Use inertia ring when necessary to stall for time as your team kites away and you are too far to use E/E is on cooldown.

title: Bedrock mace defensive stopper
author: mystisksang
description:
Prevent engages on team/backline using Snare Charge and Force of Nature. Demon Armor should be used on enemy burst and knight armor to prevent engages on chokes.
Try to position E at an angle that will block off chokes or to stall them for longer if possible.

title: Heavy Mace purge stopper
author: mystisksang
description: Primary role is to use Snare Charge and Battle Howl to stop enemy engages. Battle Howl will purge buffs from enemies and silence for a few seconds (scales with IP).

title: Earthrune primary engage
author: mystisksang
description:
Initiate most engages with Human W (Positional Drift), followed by golem W.
Engage uses no shift charges, but shift charges will increase maximum hp in golem form.
Human Q swappable between Q3 and Q4 by preference.

title: Primal Staff Stopper and Defensive
author: mystisksang
description:
Stack 4 shift charges with shield Q on self or allies. If playing front, swap to Q4 and Caerleon Cape.
Head can be replaced with Helmet of Valor depending on comp.

title: Holy Staff (Healer) PVE Group Build
author: Agnoxia
description:
*Absolute Priority: The Tank                                                                                                           --Your number one priority will always be the tank. If the tank dies, the whole team (you, DPS and support) will most likely die as well.
-Even if a DPS takes damage (from an area or anything on the map), if the tank is also taking damage, your focus should be on the tank first. If you can heal the DPS without putting the tank at risk, do so, but the tank is the priority.                                    -DPS are assumed to dodge damage; if a DPS takes damage from an area, it is their responsibility and not the tank's or yours as the healer.       

*Aggro Management:
-It is crucial that you do not heal the tank before he "hits" monsters with an ability (Q, E or W). If you do, you will steal aggro from the mobs and disarm the entire pull, which can be catastrophic.             
-There is a way to heal the tank without stealing aggro: using the "Calm" potion. By activating Calm, you become invisible to monsters, allowing you to heal the tank without being detected and without disarming the pull. After using Calm, you can cast "Grave Guard Helmet".

*Healer Skills and Strategies
 ◦Use of skills:
▪Throw a Q or EQ when the tank ‘hits a Q’ on bugs.
▪Throw a W when the tank does a large pull or smaller pull.
▪Use the ‘guardatumba helmet’ for powerful heals.
▪ ‘Druid's Habit’ is useful for granting mana to the party and yourself.                            ▪ Healer's Passive: After four skills, buff your heals by 20%.                                                    ▪ If you can be close to your other allies (DPS, etc.) when you cast your real jacket even better so it takes advantage of the 50% CD reduction.     
Combo: Jacket + Helmet + W + Q + E (or the other way around if you want the latter two) and keep spaming the first skill as the more you apply them the more your healing increases by ‘Q’.

title: Warbow Solo Roaming and Corrupted Dungeon Build
author: Remile
description:
# The Warbow Hunter
This Build is fairly cheap but effective, you can use it for Roaming, Mists and Corrupted Dungeons as well.
The Main Build (**Soldier Helmet / Soldier Boots**) are more versatile and aiming for more survivability than Damage. The Alternative is the opposite with **Mage Cowl** and **Assassin Shoes** going for the Damage and Cooldown Reduction.

# Capes
- **Thetford Cape**
Used for better PvE Performance, but also quite helpful for some extra Damage and it is cheap.
- **Undead Cape**
Gives the Edge when aiming purely on PvP Content.

# Weapon Spells
- **Multi  Shot**

title: Light Crossbow Ava Gold Chests
author: TutoriAlbion
description:
PT/BR: A Light Crossbow / Besta leve  tem uma sequência de habilidades para extrair o máximo de dano na sua rotação.
Aqui vou colocar só os botões de ação, e depois você pode treinar na sua ilha, vamos lá:

R, E, Q, Q, Q, W, F, Q, Q, W, D, Q, Q.

Só para você entender o que aconteceu:
A Besta tem uma passiva que reseta o "Q" quando usa 4 habilidades. A Capa de Caerleon também reseta o "Q" em um determinado tempo.
Então quando você usa essa sequência, é possível usar 4x o "Q", aumentando o seu dano nos mobs!
Depois de fazer todo esse combo, você vai alternando as skills mas sempre usando o "Q" quando tiver no 4º stack da passiva.
Parece difícil, mas é só questão de treino!

EN: The Light Crossbow has a sequence of skills to extract maximum damage in your rotation.

Here I'll just put the action buttons, and then you can train on your island, here we go:

R, E, Q, Q, Q, W, F, Q, Q, W, D, Q, Q.

Just so you understand what happened:

The Crossbow has a passive that resets the "Q" when you use 4 skills. The Caerleon Cloak also resets the "Q" after a certain amount of time.

So when you use this sequence, you can use the "Q" 4x, increasing your damage on mobs!

After doing this whole combo, you'll alternate the skills but always use the "Q" when you have the 4th stack of the passive.

It seems difficult, but it's just a matter of practice!

title: Shadowcaller Ava Gold Chests
author: TutoriAlbion
description:
PT/BR: O Chama sombras deve usar seu "E" no TANK quando ele agrar os mobs, em seguida use o Elmo de Espreitador "D" para aumentar o dano do grupo, o "W" para  reduzir a resistência do mob e o "Q" para ajudar no DPS.
Ative o Casaco Real para resetar as skills do seu grupo.
Você também pode usar as Sandálias de Sectário "F" para reduzir a defesa e cura do MOB, mas precisar ficar do lado dele.

EN: Shadowcaller should use his "E" on TANK when he buffs the mobs, then use the Stalker Helmet "D" to increase the group's damage, the "W" to reduce the mob's resistance and the "Q" to help with DPS. 
Activate the Royal Coat to reset your group's skills. 
You can also use the Cultist Sandals "F" to reduce the MOB's defense and healing, but you need to stay on his side.

title: Hallowfall Healer Ava Gold Chests
author: TutoriAlbion
description:
PT/BR: Use o  Elmo de Guarda-Tumbas somente quando Tank estiver com pouca vida!
Lembre-se que a cura prioritária é sempre no Tank, o restante do grupo precisa desviar das habilidades dos mobs.
O Robe Real pode ser usado na segunda rotação de Skills para potencializar o dano do grupo.
E por fim, o Healer não precisa ficar junto do grupo, podendo se posicionar mais para o lado e um pouco perto do tank, mas longe o suficiente dos mobs.

EN: Use the Graveguard Helmet only when the Tank is low on health!
Remember that the priority healing is always on the Tank, the rest of the group needs to dodge the mobs' skills.
The Royal Robe can be used in the second Skill rotation to increase the group's damage.
Finally, the Healer does not need to stay with the group, and can position himself more to the side and a little closer to the tank, but far enough away from the mobs.

title: Light Crossbow Solo PvP Build
author: WickedUwU
description:
- **Core rotation**  
  Keep spamming **Q** and **W** on the enemy. Use **E** whenever it's off cooldown.  
  You **must maintain 3 stacks** on your passive to enable double **Q** casts.

- **Recommended combos**  
  - `Q → W → E → Q → Q`  
  - Then follow with: `Q → W → Q → Q` or `Q → E → Q → Q`  
  The main goal is to **keep 3 stacks** at all times.

- **Boots usage**  
  Boots won’t help much with chasing. This build is designed to **operate on low HP**—you either **sprint out** or **stay in and melt the enemy** with the boots’ buff active.

- **Survivability gear**  
  - **Guardian Helmet** and **Cleric Robe** provide strong protection, especially when you're low HP.  
  - Use **Martlock Cape** for extra defense when low, but be aware it may cause **energy issues**.

- **Energy sustain**  
  If using Martlock Cape, swap your offhand to **Eye of Secrets** to help with energy regeneration.

- **Boots alternatives**  
  Consider **Soldier Boots** with **Rejuvenating Sprint** if you want more survivability, but note that you'll lose out on damage potential.

title: 1H Spear Solo PvP Build
author: WickedUwU
description:
- **Poke and kite**  
  Keep your distance and stack up using **Q**.

- **Frontline trading**  
  Brawl with **Inferno Shield** for pressure. Use **W** to gain resistance against heavy damage and reflect it back.

- **Disengage with E**  
  Use **E** defensively when the enemy:  
  - Pops sustain abilities  
  - Uses a sprint to gap-close

- **Engage with E**  
  Use **E** offensively to:  
  - Chase  
  - Interrupt abilities  
  - Execute low HP targets

- **Helmet utility**  
  Your helmet ability can:  
  - Cleanse damage-over-time effects  
  - Save you at low HP

- **Escape plan**  
  **Undead Cape** gives you a second chance—pair it with boots and **E** to escape cleanly.

title: Frost Staff PvE DPS Build for Gold Chests
author: TTHORG
description:
Arctic is the preferred option but more expensive. Chillhowl is the same dps as 1h frost realistically, but can provide your tank some possibly much needed invulnerability. Perma is the worst dps option of these 4 frost staffs, but it's usable if your team is planning on mixed pvp/pve. Switch to scholar robe only if you're on perma and planning on pvp. Use Q1 on bosses.

If you bring scholar robe to a PvE speed clear gold chests team, you hate yourself and your team. 

Most of your DPS comes from using Ice Shard(Q2), so I often say that any frost staff is fine.

title: Shadowcaller PvE DPS Build for Gold Chests
author: TTHORG
description:
Focusing on DPS is better. The utility bot variant for Shadowcaller(Hellion Hood-Royal jacket-Mistcaller is a suboptimal crutch for low dps teams). They'd be better off with a GA on empowering beam IMO. If you use Shadowcaller for utility, you hate yourself, your team hates you, and you hate your team.

Self cast E always. If you think otherwise, please look up how resistances work, and how much armor/magic resist Group content mobs have. If you've done that, and still believe in pierce... We'll just agree to disagree then.

Spectre and Stalker jacket can be usable as well, but for nearly all PvE DPS, druid robe is best.

title: Utility Bot Great Arcane Build for PvE and Gold Chests
author: TTHORG
description:
Use empowering beam on your highest non-Ironroot dps. Use Time Freeze(E) on mobs on command. Bring a druid cowl swap. GA sets are often the cheapest right next to ironroots, so it could be the best case scenario for you to sacrifice yourself for your team against divers

I recommend this over the more commonly seen Shadowcaller with Stalker Hood/Hellion hood-royal jacket- cultist sandal build. Great Arcane Staff provides much more utility and does much more damage than a utility shadowcaller

There are no requirements for cape. Demon cape is useless. Lymhurst cape might be the best option if druid cowl isn't needed.

title: Mistpiercer PvE Build for Gold Chests
author: TTHORG
description:
Taking scholar robe is suboptimal for dps. Keep one on you as a swap for possible pvp encounters as it'll be too difficult to stack druid robe on demand.

Druid robe, assassin's hood, and Morgana cape are for the highest damage output. At a certain point, clear speed is capped by cooldowns rather than damage. Royal hood then becomes pointless, but can be usable.

If your dps is lower than with the more commonly seen scholar robe-royal hood build, dm me with proof in game and I'll give you 1m silver

title: Infinity Blade Backline Dive - Crystal Arena
author: Khizzixxx
description:
Build is intended to be backline dive, your main target with this build is and always should be the enemy healer. 

Your cape slot can either be Thetford or Avalonian, i personally use the thetford over the avalonian because of the quicker cooldown for more overall dps when attempting to stick to a healer and burn their health/mana.

Rotation for engaging, look to see if you can engage on the enemy healer to begin with, if you can not get onto the enemy healer look to poke opponents with your 1 weapon ability ( Q ) and back out to your healer. 

If you are able to dive into the backline and engage on the healer, you should look to open with your Q as you would the poking stage. Your weapon ability 3 ( E ) is used for helping close gaps as well as giving you a massive damage buff for 5 seconds. 

if you get onto the healer look to use skills as followed:
Chest >  Boots >  AA >  Weapon 3 >  AA >   Weapon 1 >  AA >  Weapon 2 >  AA ~ Use skills on cooldown as needed from this point. 
(AA is Auto Attack)

Your helmet is a powerful tool allowing you to purge many meta items such as Hellion Jackets and Cleric Robe as well as a lot of move speed boot options, it is a targetable AoE that both purges as well as cleanses allies. Try to save it for possible Cleric Robe on healer if needed and possible. If that's not necessary i recommend mainly using it as a cleanse tool for your team.

The recommended setup is if you have a healer that is willing to dive/semi dive the backline with you. If you dont have a healer willing to "go in" with you I would highly recommend using the alternate build path, so having a swap set is very helpful in my personal opinion.

(This build is a work in progress, im currently Gold 2 this season and have solo queue climbed with this setup and playstyle.)

title: Permafrost Prism Fame Farm Avalon Group Build
author: Harjulf
description:
To start, **NO**, don’t use reduced cast time passives on your armor — it doesn’t work like you think it does. You get **Speed Buffs** from specific items like **Morgana Cape**, **Passive 3** on your weapon, and **Speed Caster** from **Scholar Robe**. Otherwise, focus on **all damage passives**. If you think you need more speed, you're not playing it right, period.  

You also get a **speed buff** from your **Omelette**.  

**How to play Perma:**  
1. Use **Glacial Obelisk** to buff your team.  
2. Before dropping your abilities, do **R > E > QQQQQQQQQQ**.  

Simple.

description:
This is the **META healing build** for **Constructs** right now:  

- **Fiend Robe** to **interrupt Macaras** and their buffs.  
- **Mercenary Shoes** to break free from snares and stuns.  
- **Invis** or **Calming** to escape the chest if needed.

title: Blazing Staff Fame Farm Avalon Group Build
author: Harjulf
description:
In every **Gold Chest comp**, there's always a **Blazing**, as it’s typically the **highest DPS** in the group and the **pure DPS build**.  

As a **Blazing**, your job is to **interrupt every pack** except **The Construct**, where interrupts aren’t needed.  

- **Before every pull**, spawn your **Royal Robe** on the opposite side of where the tank pulls, so the other DPS can stand in it.  
- **Interrupt priority:** Stop the **Macaras** from buffing themselves and the **Archers** from using **Rain of Arrows** as quickly as possible.

title: Blazing Staff Crystal Arena Glass Cannon Build
author: Harjulf
description:
This build is designed **only for the initial engage**, unless it goes extremely well. It’s a **glass cannon**, so your goal is to deal massive damage and reset.  

**Engage Sequence:**  
1. **Prep** your **Royal Hood**  
2. **Pop** **Royal Sandals**, **Berserk Potion**, and **Scholar Robe**  
3. **Use E**, followed by **Fire Artillery**  

After that, reset unless the enemy team is severely weakened—**you die easily** if you overstay.  

**If You Die or Need to Swap:**  
- **Play defensively** and swap abilities to **Fire Wall, Burning Field, and Passive 1**  
- If you have a **strong healer or tank to peel**, you can keep pushing—the damage is so high it’s hard to counter without enemy support.  

**Important Note:**  
This is **not an ideal Crystal Arena build**—it's meant for fun. It **can work** and be devastating, but it’s too fragile for serious top-tier Arena matches.

title: Druidic Staff Solo Fame Farm Build
author: Harjulf
description:
This is a **definitive fame farming build** for **Druidic Staff**.  

**Key Playstyle:**  
- Use **Revitalize** with **Cleric Robe's special ability** for a **full heal** or between attack timers.  
- **Soldier Armor** helps block damage, making you tankier.  
- **Scholar Sandals** sustain mana, but you can switch to **Cultist Sandals** if mana isn’t an issue.  
- **Torch** boosts attack speed, helping **Q2 (Thorn Growth)** deal more damage and restore more energy (**Energetic passive**).  

**Optional Gear:**  
- **Lymhurst Cape** and **Demon Cape** aren’t required but can help with **sustained farming**.  
- **Cultist Cowl** adds extra damage and speeds up clears, but **dodging and patience** are more important.  

**Proven Performance:**  
This build can **clear T8 Solo Encampments and Roads Green Chests** even on **4.2 gear** without a special cape.  

**Happy farming!**

description:
Important information about the build:

Always use your Q twice to buff the damage of your basic attack. Always combo your basic attack with your skills.
I like to use W Fleet Footwork to combo with my Mercenary Jacket, because that way the enemy won't be able to counter my healing. For example, if the enemy is invisible or has a purge, you can avoid this by using your E+R+W and do exactly this combo quickly, so the enemy won't have time to react and won't be able to counter you because he'll be in W's group control, so you'll heal all the Mercenary Jacket stacks. I also like this W to finish off enemies in the Undead Cape, to do this you can use your E+W+Q so the cape will activate but the damage will still be on him.
Have fun with the build :) Watch the video to learn more!

title: Redemption Staff Duo Mist Build
author: ZombieNinjaGod
description:
This build is most effective when played alongside a dedicated tank. Your primary role is to stay close to the tank, providing support through shielding and healing while maintaining resource efficiency.

Positioning: Stay near the tank at all times to ensure that your heals and shields benefit both of you. This is especially crucial when anticipating enemy stuns or high-damage abilities.

Healing Management: Avoid excessive healing—allow your health to drop slightly before using abilities. The healing orb provides a substantial burst of healing when used at close range, potentially restoring almost full health in critical moments.

Cooldown Optimization: The Omelette reduces cooldowns, allowing you to cycle through your abilities quickly. Combined with your three shields, you can mitigate incoming damage efficiently during brief downtime.

Sustainability: The Lymhurst Cape and energy potion ensure sustained mana regeneration, allowing you to maintain your healing output over extended engagements.

Survivability & Endurance: By carefully timing your shields and managing cooldowns, you can outlast opponents in prolonged fights, making this build highly effective in attrition-based encounters.

title: Holy Staff Solo Fame Farm Build
author: ZombieNinjaGod
description:
This build offers a strong balance of mobility and sustained damage, allowing you to engage effectively while maintaining resource efficiency. With Beef Stew, your damage output increases significantly, enabling you to stay on the move while dealing consistent damage.

Damage Rotation: Activate Obsessive Burst, then use Smite six times to reach maximum damage potential. Follow up with Fire Breath and Sacred Pulse in that order to apply damage-over-time (DoT) effects while continuing to use Smite for steady damage. 

Mobility & Positioning: If avoiding an attack is not possible, use Shield Charge to move toward your target. Follow up with Sacred Pulse to either interrupt the attack or push enemies away, helping you to continue dealing damage.

Burst Damage: The Caerleon Cape provides a free double-damage boost approximately every 45 seconds, significantly enhancing your overall damage.

Resource Management: Energy Potions should recharge in time between uses to keep your energy levels stable. If planning to engage large groups of mobs, consider switching to the Lymhurst Cape for additional energy regeneration.

Defensive Adaptation: If energy management is under control, use a Resistance Potion for extra defense during cooldowns, ensuring greater survivability in tougher encounters.

With proper ability timing and positioning, strong burst damage, and sustained efficiency, making it highly effective for a variety of encounters.

title: Great Arcane Mid-Scale Build
author: Husansko
description:
This build is flexible and adaptable for various scenarios in Albion Online.  

- **Stalker Shoes** are the best for mobility, letting you catch and set up clumps with double blink. If preferred, **Cleric Sandals** can be used instead.  
- **Feyscale Sandals** are a great alternative in larger fights, helping you rejoin the zerg after using your chest spell.  
- **Armor choice depends on your team:** **Duskweaver** is ideal for kite comps, while **Knight Armor** offers better protection against dive-heavy opponents.  
- **Weapon passive:** Switch to **Lingering Power** for extra hammering damage in sieges or **Calmness** if the enemy lacks a Beetle or Ballista to silence.  
- **W spell slot:** In large-scale battles, consider **Mimic** to copy powerful abilities like **Inertia Ring, Battle Rush, or Guard Rune**, depending on the situation.

author: Nihalz
description:
Your main role with this setup is to dive into the opposing team's backline and target their healer and ranged DPS. While you're durable and have lifesteal, it's crucial to retreat to your healer when needed.

This build shines in duo or trio setups, where coordination is easier, but it's less effective in premade 5v5 teams. In those situations, a well-coordinated enemy team can easily counter you.

author: Nihalz
description: Build up your stacks while maintaining distance. If possible, charge your fury using chest active skills. Once ready, start spamming your Qs and auto-attacks to take full advantage of your weapon's passive. Learn to time your W in bird form effectively, especially in clumps and chokes, to maximise its impact.

title: Battleaxe Open World PVE/PVP Build
author: Matheus Dragneel
description:
Have a balance between power and cost-benefit. I recommend this build for doing solo PVP/PVE content in the open world, such as camps or dungeons. While you do this, you can kill other players who are farming camps or just gathering resources. Use the invisibility potion to get to these players without them noticing. Your Fiend Cowl helmet is an important piece to keep these players from escaping, as its ability will nullify their boots, so use it at the right time.

You can use Muisak as an alternative to Off-Hand, but you will spend a lot of mana doing PVE, which is why I opted for the torch, which is cheap and keeps my mana stable.
